`lib/cyrus/import` + `services/modbuilder/import.js`: source-only. Copies `src/main/{java,resources}`, ignores the uploader's build files (their build is never run), compiles with the service template and a **curated checksum-pinned dependency allowlist** (`import/deps.json`; first-class integrations Vault, LuckPerms, PlaceholderAPI). Unsupported: Kotlin, Lombok, annotation processors. Ingestion limits (zip-slip, zip-bomb ratio, nested jars, multi-release, class major), no execution at ingestion, ownership attestation record, detected licence, public sharing hard-off. Two scan profiles: strict for generated, **attested/imported** with warnings and no "safe" claim. Imported source becomes revision 0 and uses the same change planner, tests, versions and install path. Jar-only imports are analysis only. Not plan-gated (model use and assets follow tokens and gates). Flag `cyrus_import_enabled`. Fixed: import refused 1.21.9+ data packs (r31).

## Data packs and worldgen
`lib/cyrus/datapack`, `services/modbuilder/{datapack-spec,datapacks}.js`, `scripts/cyrus/datapack-derive.py`: a typed spec compiled by per-version emitters (the AI never hand-writes JSON); schema source vanilla-mcdoc (MIT); static validation (including a command allowlist and `line_continuation` refusal) then a real headless Paper over RCON. Content: recipes, loot tables, advancements, tags, functions, enchantments (value effects, and since mc-coverage `postAttack` entity effects + `attributes`), damage types, jukebox songs (music discs), predicates and item modifiers (mc-coverage; real flights on 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/1.21.11, `mc-coverage-datapack-flights-2026-10-11.json`). **Worldgen** (R4: custom dimensions, biomes, structures; `CYRUS_WORLDGEN`): `/reload` does not reload worldgen, so these need a restart and a **broken worldgen pack stops a server at its next start**; hence delivery rollback is mandatory. Spans four datapack schemas and two `pack.mcmeta` styles (`min_format/max_format` from 1.21.9). Verified: worldgen showcase passed on 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/1.21.11/26.1.2/26.2; broken files each alone (validator 8/8, server refuses to start 7/8). Flags `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO`, `CYRUS_WORLDGEN`.

## Creatures
`lib/cyrus/creature` + `services/modbuilder/creatures.js` (`CYRUS_CREATURES`): `RigSpec` (3 archetypes, 5 procedural clips, 32 bones/creature, 4 creatures per server caps) compiled to a Blockbench `.bbmodel` for the Nxeon-managed **BetterModel**: 3.5.0 (Java 25) for 26.x and, since mc-coverage, **2.2.0 (Java 21) for 1.21.x** (same API; a Cyrus-compiled banshee flew on real Paper 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/1.21.11 with seeded runtime libraries, `bettermodel-121x-flights-2026-10-11.json`; registry `animatedCreatures` on every buildable version; compile-only deps `bettermodel-api-2`/`bettermodel-bukkit-api-2`; managed config `bettermodel-2.2.0-config.yml`). Base vanilla mob supplies hitbox/AI; display entities carry the bones. Do not embed Blockbench (GPL). Verified on real Paper 26.2: load, pack hand-off + Pack Loader, malformed models, perf ramp 1/10/50; r30: creature paint is byte-identical inside BetterModel's pack. Not verified: how it looks or animates in a real client.

## Gameplay designers
All behind `CYRUS_DESIGNER` (+ `CYRUS_DESIGNER_BUILDS` for no-model builds). Design files live in `assets/designs/<id>.json` with a top-level `kind`; the compiler (`lib/cyrus/designer`, 39 files) emits a complete Paper plugin from a **verified Java component library**; every number/text becomes a `config.yml` setting, so edits change config only (proved with a config migration on real servers). Static + runtime **Budget** caps, no `run_command`, no arbitrary scripts. Javadoc/escape injection fixed in r32 (AC-3).
- **Item + ability graph (R3)**: 10 triggers, 11 conditions, 21 actions, 17-component library.
- **Menu + quest (R3)**: chest menus (click/drag cancel hardening, pagination, item/XP/Vault money prices, permissions, dialogues), quests (chains, 7 objective kinds, branches, daily/weekly, per-player progress in PDC).
- **Boss + encounter (R4)**: 20 vanilla bases, 1-5 one-way phases, up to 8 telegraphed attacks, arena (leash, enrage), boss bar, capped minions, drops by damage share, wave encounters; never persistent, no griefing.
- **Boss model (2026-10-15, branch `feature/cyrus-boss-model`, not merged; build-service switch `MB_BOSS_MODEL`, default OFF)**: a boss design can WEAR a creature rig of the mod: `"model": {"rig": "<creature name>", "scale"?: 0.5-2, "clips"?: {"attack"|"hurt"|"phase"|"death": "<clip>"}, "sounds"?: {"hurt"|"death"|"attack"|"ambient"|"spawn": "<key>"}}`; minions (`summon.rig`) and encounter wave mobs (`spawns[].rig`, with `entity` only) too. The base `entity` keeps the AI, attributes and hitbox; it is made silent + invisible, its hitbox (scale attribute) follows the model's height, BetterModel plays the rig's looping idle / walk itself and the boss runtime plays attack (each cast), phase (default: the attack clip), hurt (+ red tint) and death (model closed 3 s later); trackers close on despawn, death, unloaded chunk (sweep), and disable. Only mods that wear a rig get `designer/BossModels.java` (the one class using `kr.toxicity.model.api`, members javap-checked in BOTH BetterModel 2.2.0 and 3.5.0), `depend: [BetterModel]` and the version's compile-only API deps (`bettermodel-api-2`/`-bukkit-api-2` on 1.21.x, `bettermodel-api`/`-bukkit-api` on 26.x); every other boss mod has no BetterModel reference (the hub hooks stay dormant). **Fallback, explicit:** a rig the mod does not have = warning `rig_unresolved` and a vanilla body (no BetterModel at all, README note); BetterModel running but the model not loaded on the server = the vanilla body comes back (visible, with its own sounds)
- **HUD + glyphs (R4)**: action bar, per-player boss bars, per-player sidebar (never replaces another plugin's), plus the mod's own font `<ns>:hud` with codepoints from the identifier registry; 15 glyph presets; no shaders, no free positioning (the router says so).
- **Weapon components (2026-10-12, branch `feature/cyrus-mc-testing-weapons`, not merged)**: three item-designer actions with their own component `designer/Weapons.java` (`lib/cyrus/designer/components/weapons.ts`), added only to mods that use them so every existing designer jar stays byte-identical. `hitscan` (range 1-64, damage per pellet, pellets 1-12, spread 0-15 degrees on a fixed sunflower pattern, rays stop at the first block, pellet damage SUMMED per target and dealt once after `setNoDamageTicks(0)`, optional tracer particle and per-target actions); `beam` (range 1-32, pulses every 2-20 ticks for 10-100 ticks, follows the aim, the first entity on the ray takes each pulse, one beam per player, at most 16 live, ends when the item leaves the hand, no timer: a chain of single delayed steps behind the re-entry guard); `area_blast` (radius 1-8, linear falloff to 0 at the edge, players take `playerScale` (default 0.5), never the user, at most 16 targets, line of sight, optional knockback; no explosion and no block change). Lag-bomb proof: every ray spends one action of the 64-action budget, hits spend entities (32), particles come from the 512 budget; a click-triggered weapon needs `cooldownTicks >= 4` (or charges). **Full-auto is not possible server-side**: the client repeats a held right-click only every 4 ticks and sends no held state; real full-auto belongs to the client-mod lane. Real: javac 0 warnings and strict scan clean on 1.21.1 / 1.21.4 / 1.21.8 / 1.21.11 / 26.2; 
- **Technique components (2026-10-12, branch `feature/cyrus-mc-techniques`, not merged; behind `CYRUS_MC_TECHNIQUES` (portal) / `MB_MC_TECHNIQUES` (build service), both OFF: a design using them is refused with `technique_off`, the palette and the prompt never offer them).** (1) Trigger **`break_block`** (`blocks: ores|logs`, `types`) + action **`vein_break`** (vein miner / tree capitator, component `designer/Veins.java`, `components/veins.ts`): every extra block is broken AS the player with `Player#breakBlock` (a BlockBreakEvent: a protection plugin's cancel keeps the block and the vein never spreads from it), only where `World#isChunkLoaded` (never loads a chunk), at most 48 blocks (each one action of the 64 budget), 16 per tick in a 1-tick step chain behind the re-entry guard, radius 12, one vein per player and 16 plugin-wide; filters refuse containers / block entities / unbreakable blocks (`VEIN_DENY`); the shared `Trigger` enum gets `BREAK_BLOCK` only in mods that use it (every other mod byte-identical). (2) Action **`capture_mob`** (`designer/Captures.java`): an empty item catches the clicked mob as a Paper `EntitySnapshot` string in its PDC plus a random token; the server keeps token -> SHA-256 in `plugins/<mod>/captures.yml` (<= 2048), so a copied full item releases once and an edited one never; runtime deny list (non-Mobs, bosses, elder guardian, warden, giant, riders, leashed, someone else's pet). Real: javac + strict scan clean on 1.21.1-1.21.11 + 26.2; Paper 1.21.1
- **Sheets "More events and methods" block (2026-10-12)**: 89 javap checks (`sheets/api-facts.json` -> `verify-api-facts.py` on node-2 -> `api-facts.verified.json`), rendered per version by `gen-sheets.py` (only what that jar has, a NOT-in list, not-cancellable notes, pack formats from each vanilla jar), plus flight-verified behaviours on the 1.21.11 sheet only. 13 new rules (version traps, per-player border on respawn, damage attribution).
- Verified by Test Flight RCON on 1.21.11 (JDK 21) and 26.2 (JDK 25): item, menu/quest, boss (55 RCON + 2 log checks), HUD (22 checks); scripted Mineflayer player 5/5 for the boss. Not verified: a real client seeing menus/HUD/bosses; other versions have no javac classpath for designers.
- **Designer edits reach servers (r31)**: no-model designer builds (config.yml-only = the base jar repacked with only config.yml changed; structural = javac) + delivery; real flight: edit -> build -> deliver -> RCON shows cooldown 100 and config migrated v1 -> v2. Image rebuild needed before enabling.

## Build pipeline and the build service
- **Service** `services/modbuilder` (Docker image on VM 88001; see [07 operations](07-operations.md)): `server.js` (HTTP), `prompts.js`, `route.js` (complexity routing, tiers), `precheck.js` + `rules/failure-rules.json` (50 reviewed rules, `rules-2026-10-12.3`), `sheets/` (per-version API sheets), `autofix.js` (deterministic fixes before a model repair), `scan.js` (bytecode + source safety scan), `jar.js` (reproducible jars: `jar --date`, sorted inputs), `release.js`, plus asset/designer/datapack/creature/config modules that bundle the `lib/cyrus` validators. Builds run Claude CLI with Read/Write/Edit only in a throwaway workspace, `javac --release N -proc:none` against a pre-resolved Paper-only classpath (Gradle only builds classpath files), no network for the model.
- **Models by tier**: Katara = Haiku class, Saka = Sonnet, Yakko = Opus (`MB_TIER_*`); complexity routing picks cheaper models for simple requests; repairs escalate one tier after two failed repairs. Knobs (all off by default): `MB_EFFORT`, `MB_CACHE_TTL`, `MB_DEDUPE`.
- **Portal side** `lib/modbuilder/create.ts` (`createModBuild`: validation, rate limits, 2-in-flight cap, token gate), `lib/cyrus/builder` (HTTP client), `lib/cyrus/follow.ts` (NDJSON re-attachable stream: stage -> `think`, `/live` draft -> `file`/`chunk`).
- **History**: service 0.3 (tuning) -> 0.4 (images the AI reads + live code) -> 0.5 (usage metering, auto-fixes, lean tools, cost knobs; branch only) -> 0.6 (networking capability manifest) -> r0+ (engine release record, asset/design/datapack/creature/config sections, catalog tools, designer no-model builds, legacy textures, JDK 25). Only 0.4 is running on VM 88001 per the last deploy; the rest requires the rebuild in the runbook.
- Verified: eval 28/28 built, 13/13 loaded on v6 (pre-programme); the programme added 178 eval prompts (harness built, **no paid run yet**). Not verified: AI output quality for texture/sound/datapack/import/designer/meshgen specs (no paid model build has run for them).

## Test Flight
`lib/cyrus/testflight` + `scripts` runner on node-2: a disposable Paper server per target version (pinned jar + sha256), boot, plugin enabled, RCON commands, `datapack list`, log matcher, clean shutdown; honest **per-check status table** (no "success" if a required stage was skipped); label "boot-tested" only where it ran. Since perf safety a **stress phase** follows the boot checks ([performance safety](#performance-safety)). Measured: 26.x boots in about 10.4-10.8 s (722-803 MB RSS), 1.21.11 on JDK 21 in 18 s (878 MB); a whole flight 12-35 s. The **gate** (`CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_GATE`, worker sweep) flies each succeeded build; `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_BLOCK_ON_FAIL` refuses installs of failed builds. One flight at a time (node-2 build lock); no container limits yet. Real flight records live in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/*flights*.json` ([09 testing](09-testing-and-verification.md)).
- **Behaviour oracle (oracle-1, 2026-10-14, branch `feature/cyrus-behaviour-oracle`, `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_ORACLE` off).** Derives what the mod should DO from its plugin.yml / config.yml / designer / data pack / rig specs (no model), flies the probes in the same flight (optional console checks + player scenarios, about 60 s max) and stores a separate `functional` record (pass / fail / not_run / not_testable per expectation, score, coverage); never changes the boot verdict. Eval stage `behaviour`. Full page: [16 behaviour oracle](16-behaviour-oracle.md).
- **Runner tf-lite-6 (2026-10-12, branch `feature/cyrus-mc-testing-weapons`, not merged).** (1) **Survival combat stress bot**: vanilla mob AI ignores creative players (verified in Paper 1.21.11 bytecode: `MeleeAttackGoal` checks `isCreative`/`isSpectator`, `TargetingConditions` use `canBeSeenAsEnemy`), so a creative bot was a false green for mobs and bosses. `stress.botMode` = `build` (creative block stress, default) or `combat` (survival: gamemode reply checked, difficulty easy, sword + food + resistance over RCON, capped waves of daylight-safe husks/spiders tagged `nxstress`, it fights the nearest foe; hits, damage taken, kills, deaths recorded). The gate picks it from the build's planned lanes (`creature`, `designBoss`) or the designer bosses flag (`stressBotModeFor`). Real: 40 hits, 9 kills, 20 TPS. (2) **Worldgen density probes** (`worldgen` check, `lib/cyrus/testflight/worldgen.ts` + `lib.js`): force-load 3x3 chunks per sample in the pack's own dimension, wait with `execute if loaded`, count with `execute in <dim> run fill <16 x <=64 x 16> minecraft:air replace <block>` (reply strings from the jars' en_us.json), judge against a stated coarse range derived from the data pack spec (max = attempts x 8 x size x chunks x 2; min 1 only when the spec promises ore in the box); the failure names the feature with measured vs expected. Destructive only in the throwaway world; a timed-out fill is never retried. Gate switch `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_WORLDGEN` (default OFF), stored as `StoredFlight.worldgen`, never blocks Install. (3) **Prove the harness can fail** (`lib/cyrus/testflight/mutants.ts`, `test/cyrus-mc-mutants-real.ts`): a plugin that throws on enable, a plugin that spins the main thread 90 ms per tick (fixture `mainthread-spam`) and a pack with its ore moved into the air must each be REJECTED by the right check with the cause named, and each good control must pass. It found a real gap: a mod that lags from the moment it enables was judged "slow host, not run"; the stress judge now samples the JVM CPU and fails a slow baseline that burns >= 85% of a core (`busyCpuPct`), keeping not_run for a starved host.

# Project Zomboid in Cyrus: readiness checklist and explainer (2026-10-08)

Status: **not live** (`soon`). Flipping it to live is the owner's decision. Branch `feature/cyrus-v6-game-zomboid`.

## What is done

- `lib/cyrus/games/zomboid.ts`: verified GameSupport (versions 42.21 → 41.78, install side `both`, plain-language install text, 17 dangerous-API rules, breakage risks with guards, outdated signals, categories, sources, unknowns) plus a `knowledge` pack (14 API-sheet lines, 12 Build 41→42 failure rules with regex detectors).
- `lib/cyrus/engine/games/zomboid.ts`: the template generator rewritten for Build 42.15+ and the 42.13 multiplayer rules (server-authoritative effects, shared timed actions, JSON translations, `ItemType`/registry ids, own script module, per-mod Lua folders, guarded fire, no map files). API check: `API-CHECK.md`.
- `lib/cyrus/games/zomboid.validate.ts`: static validator (layout, mod.info, Lua 5.1 structure lint written in TypeScript, dangerous APIs, failure rules, MP rules, script braces, JSON translations).
# 17. Engine2: pack validator, release-day API diff, 26.x readiness, method adoption

Branch `feature/cyrus-engine2` (2026-10-15). Everything here is flag-guarded and OFF by default except the two read-only tools. Research behind it: `/root/claudeskills/agent-notes/cyrus-research/CJ-engine2-2026-10-15.md`.

## 1. Spyglass second-opinion validator (data packs, resource packs)
- **What**: `services/modbuilder/spyglass.js` runs SpyglassMC (`@spyglassmc/core`, `java-edition`, `mcdoc`; all MIT) headless in a child process (`spyglass-check.mjs`) over the exact files the emitter wrote, for the build's exact Minecraft version. It reports real schema errors (unknown/missing keys, unknown vanilla ids, bad commands, wrong value types) with a fixer hint per finding. The in-house checks (`datapack-spec.js`, `lib/cyrus/datapack/validate.ts`) stay the first line; this is the version-aware second opinion.
- **Switch**: `MB_SPYGLASS` = `off` (default) | `warn` (findings become warnings on the pack, never drop it) | `enforce` (errors become problems, one bounded repair, then the pack is left out). A check that cannot run (flag off, package or data missing, version not pinned, timeout, crash) is reported as `skipped` with a reason and is **never** a pass. `/health features.spyglass` lists the versions that are ready.
- **Offline**: all upstream data is fetched ONCE at image build by `tools/fetch-spyglass-data.js` into `/opt/mb/spyglass` and verified against the sha256 pins in `spyglass-data.json` (6 versions: 1.21.1, 1.21.4, 1.21.8, 1.21.11, 26.1.2, 26.2). The child answers every `api.spyglassmc.com` request from those files; nothing leaves the image at runtime. Refresh pins: `node services/modbuilder/tools/fetch-spyglass-data.js services/modbuilder/spyglass-data.json /tmp/x --pin`, review the diff, rebuild the image.
- **Cost**: about 13 s per run (8 s with `MB_SPYGLASS_CACHE`), once per build (results are memoised by content, because the repair gate and the asset result both check). Run it only on builds that have a data pack.
- **Licence**: Spyglass and vanilla-mcdoc are MIT. The vanilla data tarball Spyglass reads is Mojang data derived by misode/mcmeta; it stays inside the build image and is never shipped to customers.
- **Resource packs**: `spyglass-check.mjs` validates any pack root (it also loads `assets/**` JSON when the `vanilla-assets-tiny` pin is present). Wiring into the texture/item-model lanes is the follow-up; the checker itself is lane-agnostic.
- **Tests**: `test/modbuilder-spyglass.test.ts` (pure parts always; the headless run needs the packages + data and fetches one version into tmp when absent).

## 2. Release-day API diff
`node scripts/cyrus/api-diff.js --from 1.21.8 --to 1.21.11 --out report.md --json report.json`

javap-based (offline; japicmp is not needed, it needs a JDK + jars the same way and adds nothing for names): diffs the public Paper API of two versions (types, constants, fields, methods, return types, newly `@Deprecated`), maps renames inside one type, then intersects with the symbols our **sheets, rules, prompts, autofix and the golden plugins** use. Output: a markdown report and a machine-readable JSON whose `candidateRules[]` are shaped like `rules/failure-rules.json` entries (`candidate: true`; a human reviews and adds them, never auto-merged). Jars: the registry's `paperServerSha256` under the testflight dir, or `paper-api-*.jar` roots (`--roots` / `API_DIFF_ROOTS`).

## 3. 26.x readiness
`npx tsx scripts/cyrus/version-readiness.ts 26.2 26.1.2 [--health health.json]` prints what is missing before a version may be `buildable`; the logic is `lib/cyrus/versions/readiness.ts` (pure, tested). `scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh` already has the `JDK25=yes` path; the golden harness now compiles 26.x with `--release 25`. The enablement plan, evidence and risks are in the CJ report. Nothing is enabled by this branch.

## 4. Method adoption
- **Evidence levels** (`lib/cyrus/evidence/levels.ts`): `static` (compiled and checked, nothing ran) < `synthetic` (MockBukkit pre-flight) < `booted` (real Test Flight) < `behaviour` (oracle / playtest / commands answered on a real server) < `client` (nothing records this yet). A skipped or not-run rung never counts; a failed rung is shown as failed. The project page shows the ladder ("How far it was verified") and each MODLOG entry carries its level.
- **Publish-check lint** (`lib/cyrus/safety/publish-check.ts`, `CYRUS_PUBLISH_CHECK` = off | warn | enforce): commands exist, dependencies resolvable, no placeholder text, licence/credit lines, config documented, no duplicate namespace/plugin name. Wired into `saveModListing` when a page goes PUBLIC; `warn` returns the report with the save, `enforce` blocks only on error-severity findings. A lint, not legal advice.
- **MODLOG** (`lib/cyrus/modlog/modlog.ts`): the per-project change log, derived from the immutable build rows (what was asked, what changed, ledger added/regressed/dropped, notices, evidence level), shown newest-first in the studio Notes tab. Append-only by construction: a new build adds an entry, existing entries cannot change.

## Image
An image bump IS needed for section 1 (new npm packages, new COPY lines, a fetch step). Dockerfile additions: `spyglass.js` (app COPY line), `spyglass-check.mjs spyglass-data.json` (own COPY), `tools/fetch-spyglass-data.js`, the fetch `RUN`, `ENV MB_SPYGLASS_DIR`, and three pinned dependencies in `services/modbuilder/package.json`. Sections 2 to 4 need no image change (portal deploy only).

Playbook version: **1.1.0** (2026-10-11). Changelog: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). Lessons: [LESSONS.md](LESSONS.md).
Owner brief 2026-10-11: onboarding a new game must be flawless and repeatable, and this document keeps improving.
Minecraft is the reference implementation. Hytale and FiveM/RedM are ON HOLD and appear only as worked case studies

## Start here

```

```
The scaffolder writes the skeleton (adapter at maturity `planned`, GameSupport stub, empty knowledge pack, eval-set

no flag. It is idempotent (an existing file is never overwritten). `--docs-only` writes only
`docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/` (use it for screening, before anyone writes code). `--manifest` prints the derived
capability manifest. Then work through `docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/TODO.md` phase by phase (generated from

#!/bin/bash
# Promote /opt/nxeon's committed HEAD to production — SEAMLESSLY.
#
#   scripts/promote-production.sh [--dry-run] [--accept-data-loss] [--install-units]
#                                 [--skip-staging-check] [--allow-dirty] [--build-local]
#
# The build NEVER happens in /opt/nxeon any more (that is what took the site
# half-down for 10-12 minutes per promote until 2026-10-01), and since
# 2026-10-07 not on this box at all: it runs on the BUILD HOST (node-2,
# nxeon-fsn1) in its capped nxeon-build-prod.slice. Instead:
#   1. a git worktree of HEAD at /tank/nxeon-deploy/production/build (ZFS pool;
#      the root disk is ~90% full) with production's .env copied in — used here
#      only for the schema, public/ and geoip data (npm install, no build);
#   2. HEAD is pushed to node-2's git mirror plus a build-time-only env (APP_URL;
#      no secrets — see scripts/lib/buildhost.sh); node-2 runs npm install,
#      prisma generate and `next build` (stall/overall watchdog, node-2's build
#      lock, 6-thread / 10 GB cap) and the finished .next is rsynced back
#      (verified: same BUILD_ID, same file list + sizes);
#   3. schema push to the production DB (additive by default — see below);
#   4. all the old post-build steps (public/ + .next/static + geoip data into
#      standalone, standalone/.env = production .env, chown for 'nxeon');
#   5. the finished .next becomes /tank/nxeon-deploy/production/releases/<id>/;
#   6. that release is booted on 127.0.0.1:3095 and smoke-tested first;
#   7. /opt/nxeon/.next (a SYMLINK to the live release) is swapped in one
#      atomic rename, nxeon-web restarted (downtime = the restart), and
#      /, a real /_next/static chunk, this build's _buildManifest.js and /login
#      must answer 200 — otherwise it AUTO-ROLLS BACK to the previous release;
#   8. only then: npm install + prisma generate in /opt/nxeon for the worker,
#      wait for in-flight PROVISION jobs (max 4 min), restart nxeon-worker;
#   9. keeps the current + 3 previous releases. Rollback any time:
#      scripts/rollback-release.sh --production [RELEASE_ID]
#
# Flags:
#   --build-local         EMERGENCY FALLBACK: build on THIS box like before
#                         2026-10-07 (node-2 unreachable/broken). Schema is then
#                         pushed before the build, as it always was.
#   --dry-run             build + stage + smoke-test only. No schema push (prints
#                         the SQL a push would run), no swap, no restarts.
#   --accept-data-loss    pass --accept-data-loss to `prisma db push`. Without
#                         it, a schema change Prisma flags as possibly
#                         destructive aborts the promote BEFORE anything changes
#                         (the old script always passed it).
#   --install-units       install changed deploy/*.service|*.timer into
#                         /etc/systemd/system + daemon-reload (default: print
#                         the diff command and the install command only).
#   --skip-staging-check  don't require staging to be up and 200.
#   --allow-dirty         build even though /opt/nxeon has uncommitted changes
#                         to TRACKED files (they are NOT included — only the
#                         committed HEAD is built).
set -euo pipefail

DRY_RUN=0; ACCEPT_DATA_LOSS=0; INSTALL_UNITS=0; SKIP_STAGING_CHECK=0; ALLOW_DIRTY=0
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    --accept-data-loss) ACCEPT_DATA_LOSS=1 ;;
    --install-units) INSTALL_UNITS=1 ;;
    --build-local) BUILD_MODE=local ;;
    --skip-staging-check) SKIP_STAGING_CHECK=1 ;;
    --allow-dirty) ALLOW_DIRTY=1 ;;
deploy-staging.sh
preview-deploy-winback.ts
promote-cyrus.sh

#!/bin/bash
# Promote a commit of the STANDALONE Cyrus app (apps/cyrus, apps/cyrus-admin) to staging or production.
# Same safety rules as promote-production.sh: build on node-2 (never in a live tree), staging before production,
# side-port smoke test of the new release BEFORE cutover, atomic symlink cutover, health-checked restart with
# AUTOMATIC ROLLBACK, worker restarted only after the web is healthy, last N releases kept.
#
#   scripts/promote-cyrus.sh --env staging|production [--app web|admin|all] [--commit SHA]
#                            [--dry-run] [--accept-data-loss] [--rollback [RELEASE_ID]]
#
# NOT ARMED TODAY. Until extraction day (platform/targets.json cyrus.mode = "standalone") every non-dry run refuses,
# and production additionally refuses unless (a) $CYRUS_ARMED_FILE exists on the deploy host (the owner creates it
# on infra-move day) and (b) staging is healthy AND already runs the same commit. Nothing here talks to production
# in --dry-run: it prints every step instead.
#
# Config: deploy/cyrus/<env>.env (non-secret; see deploy/cyrus/README.md). Every command that touches the deploy
# host goes through `on_host` (ssh, or local when CYRUS_DEPLOY_HOST=local). Tests run the whole pipeline against a
# throwaway local "host" with CYRUS_ENV_FILE=<file> and CYRUS_ALLOW_EMBEDDED=1 (test/platform-scripts.test.ts).
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/.." && pwd)"
ENV_NAME=""; APP=all; COMMIT=""; DRY=0; ACCEPT_DATA_LOSS=0; ROLLBACK=""; DO_ROLLBACK=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --env) ENV_NAME="$2"; shift ;;
    --app) APP="$2"; shift ;;
#!/bin/bash
# Instant web rollback (or roll-forward) to a kept release — no build.
#
#   scripts/rollback-release.sh --production|--staging            # previous release
#   scripts/rollback-release.sh --production|--staging RELEASE_ID # a specific one
#   scripts/rollback-release.sh --production|--staging --list
#
# Swaps the live .next symlink to that release in one atomic rename, restarts
# the web service and health-checks it (/, a real static chunk, the release's
# _buildManifest.js, /login). If that release is unhealthy it swaps straight
# back. Takes the same per-environment lock as a deploy.
#
# NOT rolled back: the worker (it runs from the live tree's git source — check
# out the old commit there and restart the worker if you need that too) and the
# database schema (pushes are additive, so the old code keeps working).
# --force is needed to deploy a release staged by --dry-run (its schema was
# never pushed).
set -euo pipefail
ENV_NAME=""; WANT=""; LIST=0; FORCE=0; TEST_CONFIG=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
#!/bin/bash
# Cyrus launch check: GO / NO-GO for a private beta and for a public launch, every gap named with the exact fix.
# READ ONLY: no writes to production, no secrets printed. docs/cyrus/LAUNCH-RUNBOOK.md, docs/cyrus/07-operations.md.
#   scripts/cyrus/launch-check.sh [beta|public] [--json FILE] [--facts]
#   exit 0 = GO for the requested audience, 1 = NO-GO (at least one FAIL), 2 = usage.
# Run on the primary as root (reads /opt/nxeon/.env and /etc/nginx). --json also feeds the admin Launch tab:
# the hourly cyrus-launch-check.timer writes /var/lib/cyrus/launch-check.json.
set -uo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/../.." && pwd)"
case "${1:-beta}" in beta|public|--json|--facts) ;; -h|--help) sed -n 2,8p "$0"; exit 0 ;; *) echo "usage: launch-check.sh [beta|public] [--json FILE] [--facts]" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
command -v node >/dev/null || { echo "node is required" >&2; exit 2; }
exec node "$ROOT/scripts/cyrus/lib/launch-check.mjs" "$@"

# 00 Overview: what Cyrus is

Cyrus is Nxeon's AI game-mod studio. A customer describes a mod in plain language (or edits it with studios and designers), and Cyrus produces a tested, installable artifact for their game server. Minecraft (Paper servers) is the one game that is built for real today. It is a product that sits insid

> Status words used in all these docs: **live** (in production), **built** (merged into the integration branch `feature/cyrus-r2`, verified on node-2/dev host, NOT deployed), **pending** (on a branch not yet merged), **parked** (owner hold). **As of 2026-10-11 nothing from the r0..r40 programme is d

## The product in one page

- **Describe it, get a mod.** Prompt -> prompt check -> capability router -> build service (AI writes Java against a pinned Paper API) -> javac -> safety scan -> jar. Failed builds are repaired automatically (up to 3 times, cheap-first).
- **Studios** edit the same mod project without prompting: Texture, Sound, Model (viewport, paint, cuboid/bone editor, mesh retexture), Motion, Config and Stats, plus designers for items/abilities, menus, quests, bosses, encounters and HUDs.
- **Engine, not a prompt box.** A typed, versioned `ModSpec`, immutable revisions, reserved namespaces, deterministic generators, a real-server **Test Flight** (boot, RCON, playtest bots) and a delivery orchestrator with proven rollback.
- **Compose and import.** Conflict engine + Mod Packs (install and roll back as one unit), import your own mod source, data packs and worldgen.
- **Library.** A CC0-only, catalogued asset library (62k+ staged rows) with a contribution pipeline, filters and takedown.
- **Installs onto Nxeon game servers** through a scoped bridge (consent, per-server grants), or download the jar.
- **Community.** NxLabs mod pages, remixes, ratings, community-tested badge, pass-rate page.

## Plans and models

| Plan | Customer-facing model | What it unlocks |
|---|---|---|
| Free | (starter grant: one free build) | Builds only; no studios, no asset creation |
| **Katara** ($4.99/mo) | fast model (Haiku class) | Builds; no studios |
| **Saka** ($19.99/mo) | balanced model (Sonnet class) | + Sound Studio and Sound Library |
| **Yakko / "All models"** ($49.99/mo) | strongest model (Opus class) | + Texture Studio, Model Studio, Texture Library: everything |

Tiers are cumulative. Prices are from the token-economy work (2026-10-07) and are owner-changeable. Model family names are never shown to customers (a test fails if a component names them). **Mod Packs and import-your-own-mod are not plan-gated; editing numbers in the Config studio is recommended un

Tokens: 1 token = $0.002 of real AI cost (Yakko x1.25); game-server purchases and renewals grant tokens scaled by price; each month's tokens last 3 months; the ledger is append-only and idempotent with reserve -> settle -> release per build. Detail: [05 bridge and accounts](05-bridge-and-accounts.md

## Vision (owner, 2026-10-06 onwards)

1. "The ultimate game-mod creation studio", Minecraft first, other games as adapters on a game-agnostic core (Valheim, Terraria, Zomboid, Palworld, Rust, Hytale, FiveM/RedM were researched; all **on hold** since 2026-10-11 while Minecraft + bridge + cyrus.my reach 100%).
2. Stay inside Nxeon for months (one login, one wallet, one Stripe) to gather real usage data, but never build anything that cannot be separated later (the **host seam**, see [01 architecture](01-architecture.md)).
3. Engine first, evidence over claims: nothing is called built, tested or supported unless it ran; the honest limits are shown to the customer.
4. Legal hygiene is a feature: CC0-only library, no creator credit needed, game-derived material never public.
5. Looks like a premium product, not a vibe-coded add-on (see [06 portals](06-portals.md) and the design feedback in [10 decisions](10-decisions.md)).

## What the owner can see today

- `cyrus.my`: static landing page, LIVE since 2026-10-11 (served from the primary through Cloudflare; the updated landing with 8 real-time effect scenes is built but NOT published, waiting for the owner).
- Nxeon portal `/dashboard/cyrus` (the owner's v5/v6 studio, deployed 2026-10-08, preview accounts only) and `/admin/cyrus` (7-tab operating portal).
- Everything else runs only on node-2/dev host behind OFF switches.

## Map of these docs

See [README](README.md). For the "what is the state right now" question read [12 gaps and roadmap](12-gaps-and-roadmap.md) first, then [11 history](11-history.md).
# 14 How to work here

Rules for anyone (human or agent) changing Cyrus. They come from incidents and owner instructions; see [10 decisions](10-decisions.md) D-50..D-54 and [07 operations](07-operations.md) incident playbooks.

## Worktrees and devhost
- **Never edit or build in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`.** Make your own worktree on the primary: `git -C /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r2 worktree add -b feature/cyrus-rNN-<name> /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-rNN feature/cyrus-r2` (the integration branch is `
- Edit on the primary in your worktree (no `node_modules` there; never symlink one in). Run heavy things on node-2 through `/opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost`: `tsc`, `test [files]`, `build`, `run --lock -- <cmd>`, `dev`, `tunnel`, `pull`, `stop all`, `rm`. **One hea
- Throwaway DB per worktree on node-2 (`devhost db push|reset|info`). Never use production DB credentials. Forbid role/ownership SQL.
- Commit small and real. **Never `git add -A`** (name paths). Write commit messages to a file and use `git commit -F` (backticks break `-m`). End commits with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- **Never `pkill` by pattern**; stop by systemd unit or port PID.
- Never deploy, migrate production, flip flags, touch VM 88001 or customer servers, or rotate live credentials: the owner does (promote scripts: `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` then `scripts/promote-production.sh`; Cyrus: `scripts/ship`, `promote-cyrus.sh` unarmed
- No paid third-party spend (baz, model eval runs) without sign-off; no support-ticket replies without sign-off.
- Never write a secret anywhere in the repo or docs; reference where it lives (`/root/.secrets/...`, env files).

## Agent model rules and frugality
Sonnet for research and small items; Opus for big, advanced features, with a tight brief, a report path and caps; few agents; never Fable. Prefer reading existing sources over re-deriving; generate reference pages with scripts (zero model tokens: `scripts/cyru

## How to resume (after a restart or a new session)
1. Read `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/CYRUS-TRACKER.md` (first file after any restart), then [12 gaps and roadmap](12-gaps-and-roadmap.md) and [11 history](11-history.md).
2. `git -C /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r2 log --oneline -20` and `git branch --list 'feature/cyrus-r*'`; for a branch that looks unfinished, `git -C /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-rNN log --oneline` shows which items are committed.
3. Merge latest `feature/cyrus-r2` into your branch before finishing; on a conflict in a generated page, take either side and re-run the generator.
4. For a stopped agent: relaunch for the remaining items only, brief = tracker sections + item list; report to `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/<LETTER>-<name>.md` (under 400 words: what was built, RAN, NOT RUN, owner items).
5. Memory notes (`nxeon-cyrus-*.md`) hold the owner's standing preferences.

## Learning from real builds
After real builds, run the learning report and mining job and read the candidates ([15 learning loop](15-learning-loop.md)); anonymized outcome data only (D-60), candidates are reviewed and never auto-applied (D-61).

## House style for a Cyrus change
Pure core first (schema, validators, simulators, golden files), behind a flag that defaults OFF and fails closed; reach Nxeon only through the host seam; Cyrus tables through `cyrusDb`; plan gates enforced server side; honest limits in customer wording; tests;

## Docs update checklist (the LIVING RULE)
These docs must stay current "for as long as we work on Cyrus". Every merge that changes Cyrus behaviour does the following **in the same branch**:
1. **Regenerate the references:** `npx tsx scripts/cyrus/docs-build.ts` (use `--check` to verify). This updates flags/env/settings, routes, DB tables, version registry, adapters, OpenAPI operations, module map, scripts, tests, the DOCUMENTATION.md index and th
2. **Feature map:** a new feature or flag gets a row in `docs/cyrus/_data/features.json` (title, area, flags, doc, branch, state). A new flag with no obvious meaning gets a line in `docs/cyrus/_data/flag-notes.json` (a trailing `*` makes a prefix rule); admin 
3. **Narrative pages:** update the page that owns the change: engine ([02](02-engine.md)), studios ([03](03-studios.md)), assets ([04](04-assets-and-library.md)), bridge ([05](05-bridge-and-accounts.md)), portals ([06](06-portals.md)), operations ([07](07-oper
4. **Decision log:** any new owner decision gets an ID in [10](10-decisions.md) (date, why, how to apply); parked items too.
5. **History and gaps:** add the branch/commit to [11](11-history.md) (mark merged vs pending) and move anything newly verified or newly open in [12](12-gaps-and-roadmap.md). Be honest: pending / unmerged / unverified stay marked until proven.
6. **Long form:** the per-feature section in `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is still where numbers and proofs go; the Cyrus pages link to it.
7. **Run the gate:** `scripts/devhost test test/cyrus-docs-coverage.test.ts` must pass. It fails when a Cyrus flag / env var / route / table / adapter / version / OpenAPI operation exists in code but not in the generated reference, when generated pages are sta
8. **Never include:** secrets, the contents of the owner's game-asset archives, or customer data.
Lessons learned after each game onboarding go into the onboarding playbook (r47) and into [10](10-decisions.md).

# 21 Infrastructure map

One page that answers "what runs where, on which port, started by what, backed up how, and who restarts it". It is the map; the step lists are in [07 operations](07-operations.md), the owner runbook [CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK](../CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK.md) and the [28 operations handbook](28-operations-handbook.md). Unit files that exist in the repo are listed, generated, in [reference/infra-units.md](reference/infra-units.md); whether a unit is INSTALLED on a host is answered by `scripts/cyrus/launch-check.sh`, never by this page.

Evidence labels: **(repo)** = read from a file in this repo today; **(note)** = from a dated agent note or the tracker, not re-measured here; **(unverified)** = nobody has confirmed it on the live host since the stated date. No IP addresses appear in these docs (a test enforces it): hosts are named by role.

## Diagram

```
                           Internet / customers / owner browser
                                       |
                 Cloudflare zone cyrus.my (proxied; nxeon zones NOT proxied, parked D-57)
                                       |
 +-------------------------- PRIMARY  (OVH dedicated, Singapore; customer-facing) -----------------------------+
 | nginx :80/:443  vhosts: nxeon.cloud (portal + /api/cyrus + /sso/cyrus), cyrus.my (static landing + app host   |
 |                  rewrite to app/cyrus-host), admin host (secret subdomain), staging :8080                    |
 |   nxeon-web.service        Next.js 15, port 3000  ----+                                                      |
 |   nxeon-staging-web        port 3001 (DB nxeon_staging)                                                      |
 |   nxeon-worker.service     polls Job table every 3 s; Cyrus sweeps (modbuilder-sync 20 s, Test Flight gate,    |
 |                            delivery, data jobs, perf watch, webhook outbox)                                  |
 |   PostgreSQL 17  db nxeon (42+ Cyrus tables), db nxeon_staging                                               |
 |   nxeon-modbuilder-tunnel.service  ssh -L 127.0.0.1:7340 -> build VM :7340 (jump via node-2)                  |
 |   release dirs /tank/nxeon-deploy/production/releases/<id>  (.next symlink swapped atomically)                |
 |   timers: cyrus-alerts (5 min), cyrus-launch-check (hourly), cyrus-backup, cyrus-storage-report, ...         |
 |   /tank ZFS: backups, NX Labs mirror, library staging (/tank/cyrus-library-staging), packs, managed plugins   |
 |   customer VMs (never touched by Cyrus work)                                                                 |
 +----------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------+
                  | ssh (worker holds the transport)                                       | ssh -J node-2
                  v                                                                        v
 +--------- NODE-2 (nxeon-fsn1, Germany: BUILD HOST) ----------+     +---- VM 88001 "modbuilder-claudebox" (on node-2) ----+
 | scripts/devhost: tsc, tests, next build, agent dev work      |     | Docker container `modbuilder:<tag>`                |
 | prod release builds (slice nxeon-build-prod, 6 threads/10 GB)|     |   server.js on :7340 (loopback in the VM)          |
 | Test Flight: disposable Paper per flight (pinned jar+sha256) |     |   Claude CLI (API key or subscription login),      |
 | Try It controller, sound render host, Blender/meshgen        |     |   JDK 21 (+25 for 26.x), Paper API classpaths,     |
 | throwaway Postgres :5433 for agent worktrees                 |     |   MockBukkit pre-flight, Spyglass data pinned      |
 | ~13 customer VMs (never touched)                             |     |   data: /var/lib/modbuilder/data                   |
 +--------------------------------------------------------------+     +----------------------------------------------------+

 Backups out of the primary:  node-2 (gpg copy)  +  Dropbox restic repo `cyrus/restic`  +  platform DB/VM syncs to Dropbox
```

## Hosts and roles
| Host | Role | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Primary** (OVH, Singapore) | Production web, worker, Postgres, nginx, customer VMs, staging, `cyrus.my` landing, the loopback end of the build tunnel. Never build, test or run agent work here (outages 2026-10-01, crash 2026-10-06). | [07 operations](07-operations.md) "Where things run"; `/opt/nxeon/CLAUDE.md` environments section (note) |
| **node-2** (Germany) | Build host for production releases and all agent work (`scripts/devhost`), Test Flight, Try It, sound render, Blender, throwaway Postgres on port 5433; hosts the build VM; also runs customer VMs. Capped by systemd slices (`nxeon-build.slice`, `nxeon-build-prod.slice`). | `scripts/promote-production.sh` header (repo); [14 how to work here](14-how-to-work-here.md) |
| **VM 88001** `modbuilder-claudebox` | The build service container. Reached only through the tunnel unit. Image tag history in [23 build service](23-build-service.md). | `services/modbuilder/nxeon-modbuilder-tunnel.service` (repo) |
| Customer game nodes (node-4, node-5, node-7 ...) | Customer game servers. Cyrus installs mods to them only through the delivery orchestrator and the Nxeon bridge. | [05 bridge](05-bridge-and-accounts.md); memory notes (note) |
| Cloudflare | Zone `cyrus.my` active and proxied; Nxeon zones prepared but unproxied by owner choice. | [07 operations](07-operations.md); tracker 57 (note) |

## Ports and endpoints
| Port / endpoint | What | Defined in |
|---|---|---|
| `3000` | Production Next.js web (`nxeon-web`) | `deploy/nxeon-web.service.d` (repo), `/opt/nxeon/CLAUDE.md` (note) |
| `3001` / `8080` | Staging web / staging nginx listener (debug path; use the staging host name for real tests) | CLAUDE.md (note) |
| `3095` | Loopback port where a promote boots the NEW release for the smoke test before the swap | `scripts/promote-production.sh` (repo) |
| `7340` | Build service HTTP (VM loopback; the primary reaches it through the tunnel on its own loopback) | `services/modbuilder/nxeon-modbuilder-tunnel.service`, `services/modbuilder/run.sh` (repo) |
| `7341` ... | Additional build workers when `CYRUS_MB_DISPATCH=1` and `MODBUILDER_URLS` list more than one URL (no second VM exists today) | `lib/cyrus/builder/dispatch.ts`, [07 operations](07-operations.md) |
| `5433` | Throwaway Postgres on node-2 for agent worktrees (never production credentials) | [14 how to work here](14-how-to-work-here.md) |
| `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_PORT` | Loopback HTTP relay inside the worker that forwards sound render jobs to node-2 over ssh; the web process never connects to node-2 | `lib/cyrus/sound/relay.ts` (repo) |
| `/api/cyrus/health` | Portal health JSON (names the release commit via `CYRUS_RELEASE_COMMIT`) | [07 operations](07-operations.md) |
| `<service>/health` | Build service health: auth mode, `promptVersion`, features (capacity, progress, preflight, ...) | `services/modbuilder/server.js` (repo) |

## What runs on the primary under systemd
| Unit | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `nxeon-web`, `nxeon-worker` | portal and background jobs | worker restarted only after web is healthy (promote script) |
| `nxeon-modbuilder-tunnel` | `127.0.0.1:7340` to the build VM | `Restart=always`, `MemoryMax=64M` |
| `cyrus-alerts.timer` | `scripts/cyrus/alert-check.sh` every 5 minutes; writes `/var/lib/cyrus/status.json` | Discord webhook not set as of 2026-10-15 (note): alerts print to the journal only |
| `cyrus-launch-check.timer` | hourly GO / NO-GO JSON for the admin Launch tab | `scripts/cyrus/launch-check.sh public --json` |
| `cyrus-backup.timer` | nightly gpg copy to node-2 and the Dropbox restic repo | 03:40 in the repo unit; the stagger drop-in moves it to 01:30 with `TimeoutStartSec=3h` |
| `cyrus-storage-report.timer` | daily 03:40 storage report for the admin Storage tab | read only |
| `cyrus-eval-gate.timer` | weekly Sunday 04:30 eval gate (needs `CYRUS_EVAL_GATE_BUDGET_USD`) | spends model money: confirm before enabling |
| Platform timers | `nxeon-backup-vms` 04:30, `nxeon-backup-db` 03:15 (stagger), `nxeon-nightly-scan`, `nxeon-verify-restore`, Dropbox syncs, restore drills | full table in [reference/infra-units.md](reference/infra-units.md) |

## Network path of a request
1. Browser to Cloudflare (cyrus.my) or directly to nginx (nxeon.cloud). nginx on `cyrus.my` serves the static landing from `/var/www/cyrus.my` and proxies only an explicit list of app paths to the app host tree (`deploy/cyrus/nginx-cyrus-my.conf`, matrix test `scripts/cyrus/nginx-cyrus-my-check.sh`); the explicit list is **prepared, not applied** as of 2026-10-14 (tracker 107, note).
2. `middleware.ts` maps the Cyrus host to `app/cyrus-host/**`; the app itself is `app/dashboard/cyrus/**`. Sign-in is Nxeon SSO (`app/sso/cyrus/**`), see [05 bridge](05-bridge-and-accounts.md).
3. A build request leaves the web process as an HTTP call to the tunnel's loopback port; the build service answers with a build id and the portal polls (`modbuilder-sync` in the worker, 20 s cadence).
4. Test Flights are run by the worker's gate over ssh on node-2, never on the primary.

## Capacity and headroom (2026-10-15, report only, nothing changed) (note)
Source: NX hardening report section 5 (`/root/claudeskills/agent-notes/NX-hardening-2026-10-15.md`).
- **Memory:** about 62.6 GiB usable on the primary with about 5.2 GiB available and 2 GiB swap fully used; guests are allocated 100% of host RAM and ballooning keeps it afloat. ZFS ARC is capped at 8 GiB. Rule: do not start more guests on the primary until at least 10 GiB is available; use node-2.
- **Disk:** root is a 49 GB device at 87% (about 6.5 GB free). `/tank` is a ZFS pool at about 10% used, so old release directories there do not relieve the root disk. What fills root: `/root/claudeskills` (7.6 GB), Claude transcripts (4.5 GB), Postgres (5.5 GB, leave), two `node_modules` trees (5.3 GB), nginx logs (about 0.5 GB). Past incident: root disk full on 2026-09-27 crashed Postgres (about 10 minutes of 500s).
- **Build VM:** container `--memory 5g`, `MB_CONCURRENCY=2`; `auto` derives floor((memory - 600) / 1200), at most 2 per CPU. Per-build memory is a placeholder estimate, not measured on the VM ([07 operations](07-operations.md) "Build capacity").
- **Tank redundancy:** `/tank` is described in older notes as a single disk with no redundancy; the hardening report calls it a ZFS pool. Treat it as having NO redundancy until `zpool status` says otherwise (unverified).

## Backups (what, when, where)
| Layer | When (UTC) | Where it lands | Covers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cyrus-backup` (`scripts/cyrus/backup-nightly.sh`) | 03:40 (stagger: 01:30) | gpg-encrypted copy on node-2 + restic repo on Dropbox `cyrus/restic` | Cyrus DB tables, library catalogues and ledger, packs, knowledge, the proprietary SFX (51 GB), VM 88001 data and env files |
| `nxeon-backup-db` | 03:15 | local backup dir, then Dropbox databases sync 03:50 | platform Postgres |
| `nxeon-backup-vms` (vzdump about 465 GB) | 04:30 | local; Dropbox VM sync Sundays 06:30 | customer VMs |

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). # 22 Life of a build

| 11 | **Asset lanes**: textures, sounds, creature rigs, designs, data packs validated by the same typed validators the studios use; planned-but-missing lanes become a visible "laneGaps" notice | `textures.js`, `sounds.js`, `creatures.js`, `designs.js`, `datapacks.js`, `lanegaps.js` | inside step 7 (written serially in the same call) | included | nothing to overlap (CA) |
| 12 | **Release record** (engine release: prompt version, rules version, scanner sha, registry sha, ledger, progress) | `release.js`, `ledger.js` | ms | 0 | what the admin Builds tab shows |
| 13 | **Sync to the portal**: the worker's `modbuilder-sync` pulls status every 20 s; the studio follows an NDJSON stream with a live activity feed | `lib/cyrus/follow.ts`, `lib/cyrus/builder/progress-view.ts` | up to 20 s lag | 0 | feed shows files written, repair round, quiet time; a silent model is never called "stuck" |
| 14 | **Test Flight gate**: disposable Paper on node-2, pinned jar+sha256; boot, plugin enabled, commands registered, stress phase, optional worldgen probes and behaviour oracle | `lib/cyrus/testflight/**` | **median 34 s after the jar (boot 19 s)** | 0 tokens | a failed flight is a visible banner + Refine, never "featured"; `passed_with_warnings` for a failed command check |

| Lane (recorded builds) | n | Total build mean / p50 / p90 (s) | $ per build | Output tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| plain code | 68 | 74 / 52 / 152 | 0.145 | 7.8k |
| designer (item, menu, quest, boss, HUD) | 64 | 142 / 79 / 297 | 0.271 | 11.6k |
| sound | 38 | 201 / 202 / 324 | 0.369 | 20.9k |
| texture | 75 | 248 / 251 / 384 | 0.444 | 25.6k |
| owner batch (creature, recipes, wands, packs) | 11 | 300 / 282 / 455 | 0.786 | 28.7k |
| all | 257 | 171 / 150 / - | 0.326 | 16.9k |

Portal-path ranges used for the hold (CM, includes guard and repairs): light $0.36-0.55 and 2-5 min; mid $0.80-1.15 and 2-10 min; heavy $0.75-1.30 and 4-9 min; large and mega are **extrapolated** ($1.10-1.95 and $1.50-2.50, 8-20 min) because no such build had finished (the dungeon core timed out three times at the old 600 s wall clock). Budget caps in the service: `MB_CALL_BUDGET_USD` 2.5 per call, `MB_BUILD_BUDGET_USD` 4 per build (the owner's spleef build died at an earlier $1 cap: check the deployed value).

### What a token costs the customer
`cyrus_tok_tokens_per_usd` default 500 (1 token = $0.002 of AI cost), tier multipliers Katara 1, Saka 1, Yakko 1.25, minimum charge 5 tokens (`lib/cyrus/tokens/config-pure.ts`). So a $0.145 plain Saka build is about 73 tokens and a $0.786 creature batch about 393. Plan sizes (placeholders, owner to confirm): Katara 750 tokens for $4.99, Saka 3,500 for $19.99, All models 10,000 for $49.99. The owner's recommendation to move to 300 tokens per USD is open ([29 decisions](29-decisions-and-placeholders.md)).

## What can end a build early (and what the customer is told)
| Cause | Rule | Result |
|---|---|---|
| silence from the model | 300 s of no output (`MB_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S`), then ONE continuation that lists the files already written | no charge for the killed attempt beyond measured usage; honest note |
| absolute ceilings | call 14,400 s, build 21,600 s | `timeout` |
| dollar caps | call $2.5, build $4 | `budget` (customer charged for use up to the cap per settle rules) |
| AI session or rate limit | re-queue with backoff, retries 2 | `ai_unavailable` only after retries; circuit breaker holds new AI builds |
| unfixable plugin.yml `depend` | deterministic autofix or a clear failure | never "succeeded" and then fails to enable (rc12) |
| refused by guard / scan | hard | refusal reason shown; refused builds are charged by default (setting) |

## Change builds and staged mega builds
A refine sends the base build id and a workspace map plus the requirements ledger; stage chains (`CYRUS_MEGA_STAGING`, branch only, not merged as of 2026-10-15) split a request with a mega score >= 10 into editable stages, each an ordinary change build with its own hold, gates and Test Flight ([24 techniques](24-techniques-catalogue.md) lists which lanes are code cores).

## Where it is observable
- Studio: the plan card (estimate, held tokens, "Not built as the request reads"), the live activity feed, "What we verified", "Planned but not delivered".
- Admin: Builds (release record, flight verdict, errors), Live (capacity panel: slots, queue depth, p50/p80, breaker), Cost, Learning.
- Files: build records on the service, eval journals under `/root/cyrus-eval/<tag>/` (note), reports under `agent-notes/cyrus-research/`.

# 23 The build service (services/modbuilder)

The build service is a Node HTTP server inside a Docker image on VM 88001. It owns everything that touches a model, `javac`, the safety scan and the knowledge files. The portal never runs model code. This page is the map of the service: models and routing, effort, prompts and knowledge, the repair ladder, capacity, budgets and timeouts, image deploy. The complete, generated module list (every file, line count, whether the Dockerfile copies it, header comment) is [reference/build-service.md](reference/build-service.md); every `MB_*` knob with its default and meaning is [reference/flags-and-env.md](reference/flags-and-env.md).

## Request surface
`services/modbuilder/server.js` (about 2,000+ lines, the HTTP layer, build state machine, repair loop). Auth is a shared key (`MODBUILDER_API_KEY`). Main endpoints: `POST /builds` (new, change, import, designer edit, bank), `GET /builds/:id` (public view incl. `queue`, `progress`), `GET /builds/:id/live` (draft files), `POST /plan` (planner), `POST /coach` (plan-screen advice), `GET /health` (auth mode, `promptVersion`, `release.scannerSha256`, `release.registrySha256`, `features.*`, `capacity`). Contract rule: additions are additive; an old portal ignores a new field and an old service simply lacks it (the portal checks `features` before sending new fields).

## Models, routing, tiers
Defined in `services/modbuilder/route.js` (read once at start):
| Concern | Default | Env |
|---|---|---|
| Routing on/off | on | `MB_ROUTING` |
| Complexity classifier | one Haiku word (26/28 on labelled prompts, 11/12 held out), heuristic fallback | `MB_CLASSIFIER` |
| Models per class (simple / standard / complex) | all `claude-sonnet-5-5` (eval 2026-10-07: Sonnet 5.5 beat Haiku 4.5 on cost, time and first-try rate; the classifier call is skipped when all three are equal) | `MB_MODEL_SIMPLE`, `MB_MODEL_STANDARD`, `MB_MODEL_COMPLEX` |
| Customer tiers (explicit `tier` wins over routing) | Katara = Haiku 4.5, Saka = `claude-sonnet-5`, Yakko = `claude-opus-5` | `MB_TIER_KATARA`, `MB_TIER_SAKA`, `MB_TIER_YAKKO` |
| Repairs | stay on the chosen model; first repair of at most 3 compile errors goes to Haiku; escalate one tier after two failed repairs | `MB_REPAIR_CHEAP_FIRST`, `MB_REPAIR_SMALL_MAX` |
| Request guard | on; fails open if the guard errors; `strict` fails closed | `MB_GUARD` |

# 24 Techniques catalogue: how each kind of mod is made

For every mod kind Cyrus can ship: the **lane** (planner id), the **mechanism** (what actually produces the artifact), the **flags**, the **limits** the customer meets, what is **server-only vs needs the player's client**, and what is **verified** (and what is not). The depth per kind is in [02 engine](02-engine.md); the machine-readable per-version lane table and the 70-archetype matrix are in [minecraft-coverage.md](minecraft-coverage.md); the complete limits inventory is [reference/limits.md](reference/limits.md).

Policy that shapes every "limit" below (owner rule 2026-10-12, D-62 "warn, don't block"): a number a user chooses has a **recommended range with a warning**; only security, legal, money, crash, game-API ceiling and our own service capacity are **hard**. So "limit" here means "recommended maximum unless marked hard".

## The one-paragraph model
A request becomes one **plugin** (Java, compiled by `javac` against the pinned Paper API, safety-scanned, boot-tested) plus optional **assets** that ride with it: a server resource pack (textures, sounds, item models, creature models, glyph fonts) and data packs (recipes, loot, worldgen). "Designers" are not model output: the model (or the studio UI) writes a **typed JSON spec** and a deterministic compiler emits Java from a verified component library, so the same spec always gives the same code and edits change `config.yml`, not code. Creatures are the same idea for 3D rigs (a spec compiled to a Blockbench model run by the managed BetterModel plugin).

## Catalogue
Legend: **S** = server only, nothing for players to install; **P** = players accept the server resource pack; **C** = would need a client mod (not offered). Versions: 1.21.1, 1.21.4, 1.21.8, 1.21.11 buildable; 26.1.2, 26.2, 26.3 are `preview` and NOT buildable ([27 games](27-games.md)).

## Cross-cutting limits the customer always meets
- **Server-only by design.** Cyrus builds Paper/Purpur plugins and packs. Fabric/NeoForge client mods are `unsupported` (client side required); shaders, free HUD positioning, new entity/block models and full-auto weapons are outside what a server can do and the planner says so **before** tokens are spent ("Not built as the request reads", lane warnings).
- **Resource pack = a prompt for the player.** `P` kinds need the player to accept the server pack; the pack is hosted content-addressed with the Pack Loader plugin. No resource pack has been loaded by a real Minecraft client from this registry yet (`resourcePackClientVerified=false` everywhere): that is why 26.x stays preview.
- **Restart needs.** Worldgen needs a server restart; plugins need a restart (`hot reload: no`); config-only designer edits reload.
- **Performance net.** NxPerf watchdog + stress phase + post-install watch (default action `disable` + restart, TPS floor 15): see [02 engine](02-engine.md) "Performance safety".
- **Safety scan.** No `Runtime.exec`, no reflection into internals, no NMS, no network outside `net-policy.json`; a scan failure blocks the jar. Imported code gets the attested profile and never a "safe" claim.

## Vanilla techniques catalogue (research input)
`BF-mc-technique-catalogue.md` + `BF-mc-techniques.json` (2026-10-12): 156 de-duplicated techniques from the private 386-item reference corpus and the universal-modder skills; as scored that day 38 covered, 41 partial, 77 missing. Since then the following were built: survival combat bot, hitscan / beam / area blast, vein miner, mob capture, per-player effects, combat tag, armor and note-block lanes, API facts batch 2 and 13 rules ([09 testing](09-testing-and-verification.md)). Still open from the ranked list: GUI sprite skinning (boss bar, hotbar, tooltips), dialog forms as a designer kind, crates and keys, dynamic lights, menu backgrounds, lifesteal archetype, auction/escrow, jigsaw structures, skyblock/oneblock. The corpus itself is private reference (never in git, never served, never summarised here; licence handling in [04 assets](04-assets-and-library.md)).

## How a new technique is added (checklist)
1. Research note with evidence labels (V verified in repo/corpus, V-s from a source, U unverified).
2. Pure core first: spec + validator + compiler in `lib/cyrus/<lane>`; component only added to mods that use it so existing jars stay byte-identical.
3. Mirror into the build service (spec module + prompt line, ~100-130 tokens), javap-verify every API member on all buildable versions (`sheets/verify-api-facts.py`).
4. Flag default OFF; planner lane + capability catalogue row + lane-gap label; coach template if a user phrase should reach it.
5. Golden plugin + eval prompt; real Test Flight + a mutant that must fail.
6. Docs: this page, [02 engine](02-engine.md), `_data/features.json`, `doc-owners.json` rule.

The depth per kind is in [02 engine](02-engine.md); the machine-readable per-version lane table and the 70-archetype matrix are in [minecraft-coverage.md](minecraft-coverage.md); the complete limits inventory is [reference/limits.md](reference/limits.md).

Policy that shapes every "limit" below (owner rule 2026-10-12, D-62 "warn, don't block"): a number a user chooses has a **recommended range with a warning**; only security, legal, money, crash, game-API ceiling and our own service capacity are **hard**. So "limit" here means "recommended maximum unless marked hard".

## The one-paragraph model
A request becomes one **plugin** (Java, compiled by `javac` against the pinned Paper API, safety-scanned, boot-tested) plus optional **assets** that ride with it: a server resource pack (textures, sounds, item models, creature models, glyph fonts) and data packs (recipes, loot, worldgen). "Designers" are not model output: the model (or the studio UI) writes a **typed JSON spec** and a deterministic compiler emits Java from a verified component library, so the same spec always gives the same code and edits change `config.yml`, not code. Creatures are the same idea for 3D rigs (a spec compiled to a Blockbench model run by the managed BetterModel plugin).

## Catalogue
Legend: **S** = server only, nothing for players to install; **P** = players accept the server resource pack; **C** = would need a client mod (not offered). Versions: 1.21.1, 1.21.4, 1.21.8, 1.21.11 buildable; 26.1.2, 26.2, 26.3 are `preview` and NOT buildable ([27 games](27-games.md)).

## Cross-cutting limits the customer always meets
- **Server-only by design.** Cyrus builds Paper/Purpur plugins and packs. Fabric/NeoForge client mods are `unsupported` (client side required); shaders, free HUD positioning, new entity/block models and full-auto weapons are outside what a server can do and the planner says so **before** tokens are spent ("Not built as the request reads", lane warnings).
- **Resource pack = a prompt for the player.** `P` kinds need the player to accept the server pack; the pack is hosted content-addressed with the Pack Loader plugin. No resource pack has been loaded by a real Minecraft client from this registry yet (`resourcePackClientVerified=false` everywhere): that is why 26.x stays preview.
- **Restart needs.** Worldgen needs a server restart; plugins need a restart (`hot reload: no`); config-only designer edits reload.
- **Performance net.** NxPerf watchdog + stress phase + post-install watch (default action `disable` + restart, TPS floor 15): see [02 engine](02-engine.md) "Performance safety".
- **Safety scan.** No `Runtime.exec`, no reflection into internals, no NMS, no network outside `net-policy.json`; a scan failure blocks the jar. Imported code gets the attested profile and never a "safe" claim.

## Vanilla techniques catalogue (research input)
`BF-mc-technique-catalogue.md` + `BF-mc-techniques.json` (2026-10-12): 156 de-duplicated techniques from the private 386-item reference corpus and the universal-modder skills; as scored that day 38 covered, 41 partial, 77 missing. Since then the following were built: survival combat bot, hitscan / beam / area blast, vein miner, mob capture, per-player effects, combat tag, armor and note-block lanes, API facts batch 2 and 13 rules ([09 testing](09-testing-and-verification.md)). Still open from the ranked list: GUI sprite skinning (boss bar, hotbar, tooltips), dialog forms as a designer kind, crates and keys, dynamic lights, menu backgrounds, lifesteal archetype, auction/escrow, jigsaw structures, skyblock/oneblock. The corpus itself is private reference (never in git, never served, never summarised here; licence handling in [04 assets](04-assets-and-library.md)).

## How a new technique is added (checklist)
1. Research note with evidence labels (V verified in repo/corpus, V-s from a source, U unverified).
2. Pure core first: spec + validator + compiler in `lib/cyrus/<lane>`; component only added to mods that use it so existing jars stay byte-identical.
3. Mirror into the build service (spec module + prompt line, ~100-130 tokens), javap-verify every API member on all buildable versions (`sheets/verify-api-facts.py`).
4. Flag default OFF; planner lane + capability catalogue row + lane-gap label; coach template if a user phrase should reach it.
5. Golden plugin + eval prompt; real Test Flight + a mutant that must fail.
6. Docs: this page, [02 engine](02-engine.md), `_data/features.json`, `doc-owners.json` rule.
