# 15 Learning loop

Cyrus cannot fine-tune Claude. "Learning" here means **mining real build outcomes into reviewed changes** (failure rules, version-sheet facts, golden tests, routing rules, planner / guard coaching) and **shipping them as gated engine releases**. Everything below is built on branch `feature/cyrus-learning-loop`, behind `CYRUS_LEARNING` (off), not deployed. Owner decisions: [D-60 and D-61](10-decisi

## Data policy (D-60)
- **Collected by default, anonymized: outcome data only.** Per build: what kind of request (fresh / change, request length bucket, planned lanes), the lane, the model tier and family, the result (success, refused, interrupted, unavailable, failed), the fixes (repairs, attempts, autofixes), turns / cost / estimated tokens per call kind, Test Flight and install outcome, and counts of what a change r
- **Never collected into the learning data:** user mod code, imported or third-party mods, file contents, request text, class / command / config-key names, plugin names, user ids. The export record (`lib/cyrus/learning/export.ts`) carries counts where the in-memory signals carry names; build ids are opaque Cyrus ids. The mining job quotes request text or names **only** when a staff member passes `
- **Template sharing is a separate opt-in feature** and is not part of this loop.
- Retention follows ModBuild (the loop reads ModBuild, it does not copy it anywhere else).

## The loop
1. **Signals** (`lib/cyrus/learning`, pure) derive per-build outcome facts from ModBuild rows and the stored result JSON.
2. **Report** (`scripts/cyrus/learning-report.ts`) turns signals into a token-efficiency baseline with ranked levers.
3. **Mining** (`scripts/cyrus/learning-mine.ts`) clusters failed / re-requested / regressed builds into **candidates**. It never writes to the rules, sheets, prompts or router.
4. **Review**: a person reads `review.md` (or the admin Learning tab), accepts, edits or rejects each candidate. Accepting means writing the rule / sheet fact / golden case / routing change in a normal branch with tests.
5. **Gate**: the change must pass the eval harness against the accepted baseline (`evalGate` in the release manifest module: a pass-rate drop of more than 1 point blocks).
6. **Engine release**: prompts, sheets, rules, scanner and image hashes are recorded in one **release manifest** with the eval baseline reference and a rollback pointer. The manifest module is pure and **not wired to any deploy**; deploys stay with the owner (`deploy-modbuilder.sh`, D-53).

## Signals (what each one means)
| Signal | Definition |
|---|---|
| rework | the earliest later *change* of the same lineage that builds on this build (or on its base: a discard-and-retry) starts within **30 minutes** after this build ended. Upper bound of waste: a new feature request also counts. Wasted spend = this build's cost. |
| retry | a failed / refused / interrupted build re-sent word for word by the same user within 30 minutes (compared by hash). |
| regression | the change **lost commands or sub-commands, or half or more of the classes** of its base build (**major**), or lost anything smaller (**minor**). Also computed against the **last good build** of the lineage, so a chain of small drifts is caught. A config-key loss alone is minor unless both sides come from jar listings (the stored `config` list can be shorter than the real config.yml
| good / kept | succeeded, not reworked, no major regression vs its base nor vs the last good build. |
| guard refusal | `errorCode: refused` (reason from `errorDetail`, e.g. `guard:injection`). |
| interruption / unavailable | `interrupted`, or `unavailable` / `unreachable` / `lost`. |
| Test Flight failure | stored verdict `failed`, a failed check, `gave_up`, or a failed stress verdict. |
| install failure | `lastInstall` with an error. **Not recorded today** (written on success only); see gaps. |
| tier vs outcome | per Katara / Saka / Yakko: builds, kept successes, re-requests, spend, cost per success and per kept success. |
| per lane | planned lanes (`cyrus.assets.planned`) or `plain`: turns, cost, estimated tokens ($0.002 each, D-03). |

Surface (classes, commands, config keys) comes from the stored result (`files`, `commands`, `config`) or, when supplied, from jar listings (`surfaceOfJar`, `yamlKeys`). The golden fixture is the owner's ChunkMirror lineage: v1.3.0 good, then the Spawner Wand build (planner turned "mob spawner" into a designer lane and the plugin's commands and five classes disappeared) and the Haiku bolt-on that n

## Scripts
| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| `scripts/cyrus/learning-report.ts` | Read-only. One SELECT in a read-only transaction (request text hashed) or `--input rows.json`; writes the markdown report (`--out FILE`) or `--json`. |
| `scripts/cyrus/learning-mine.ts` | Same input; writes `candidates.jsonl`, `review.md`, `signals.jsonl` (anonymized), `summary.json` to `CYRUS_LEARNING_DIR` (default `./.cyrus-learning`, gitignored) or `--out DIR`. |
| `scripts/cyrus/learning-source.ts` | Shared reader (psql with `default_transaction_read_only=on`; URL from `CYRUS_DATABASE_URL`, else `DATABASE_URL`, never printed). |

Both are light and read-only, so they may run on the primary with `NODE_PATH=/opt/nxeon/node_modules /opt/nxeon/node_modules/.bin/tsx scripts/cyrus/learning-report.ts` from a worktree (never from `/opt/nxeon`). The tests run through devhost.

## Candidates
`{id, kind, title, evidence (build ids), proposedText, confidence 0-1, rationale, status: "candidate", signal}`. Kinds: `failure-rule`, `sheet-fact`, `golden-case`, `routing-rule`, `prompt-coach-gap`. Sources today: regressions (golden case "a change keeps its base's surface" + a plan-screen "keeps / replaces / removes" gap, one item per compared base), Haiku change builds that regressed on large

`lib/cyrus/learning/pathmemory.ts`: which prompt SHAPE (coach archetype + lanes + fresh / change + complexity bucket; derived ids only, the request text is read for the match and never stored in a signal or the export) went down which PATH (tier, model family, effort, starter bank / recipe / recipe holdback / plain) and what it cost: per cell n, success and kept rate, cost p25 / p50 / p90, cost pe

## 97. FIRST MEASURED BASELINE (2026-10-13, eval first1, 59 of 90 builds, 1.21.11, tier saka, $19.56; report /root/cyrus-eval/first1/report.md)
- final pass 98.3%, full pass 93.2%, real Paper boot 100% (58/58), pass@1 only 57.6%, quality 0.949, cost per pass $0.34. By lane: plain $0.15 (85% pass@1), designer $0.37 (50%), texture $0.50 (47%), sound $0.49 (17%).
- 25/59 builds (42%) needed repairs and consumed $12.76 = 65% of spend; a retried build costs about 2x. Plan-screen high estimate exceeded: texture 13/15, sound 6/6, designer 11/18, plain 3/20.
- Repair triggers (model repairs): perf pre-check hits (perf-spawn-in-loop x7, perf-block-loop x1, perf-raw-timer x1), "No design found" x7 (design lane planned, model wrote no assets/designs json), sound check problems x5, design check x3, compile errors x4, asset/texture check x3. Failures: ast-handgun-sounds q0.5, ast-handgun-textured q0.7, ast-music-disc false refusal, cov-cosmetics nothing shipped for textures.
- Rule-based lane selection (fallback, not the Haiku planner): precision 91%, recall 25%, texture 0/10.
- Fixes shipped same day: version bump for change builds (image 0.11), coach noise on plain weapons. Image 0.11 live, flags LIVE_ASSETS + MC_TECHNIQUES on both sides.
- Resumed with --in-flight 1 so interactive builds never queue. Cap $22 will stop it near 65 builds.

## 101. RELIABILITY FIX MEASURED (2026-10-13 22:10 UTC): eval second1 (image 0.13) vs first1, SAME 27 prompts
- pass@1 48% -> 88% (13/27 -> 24/27); final pass 26/27 -> 27/27; repair share of spend 78% -> 23%; cost $10.16 -> $9.44 (-7%). By lane pass@1: plain 7->8 of 8, texture 4->8 of 10, sound 0->4 of 5, designer 2->4 of 4. Cost per build barely moves because asset builds are inherently $0.4-0.5 (first attempt included); the win is reliability and waiting time. second1 continues (38 planned).

# 25 Training and knowledge: how Cyrus "learns"

**Cyrus never trains or fine-tunes a model.** It calls Anthropic models through the Claude CLI (and, for its own helpers, Haiku). Everything that makes Cyrus better over time is **engineering around the model**: what it is told (prompts, version sheets, rules), what is checked (scanner, pre-checks, goldens, Test Flight, oracle), what is reused (starter bank, recipe patterns) and what is measured (eval harness, gates, baselines). This page is the map of that knowledge: where each piece lives, who changes it, how a change is proven, and what is not learned at all.

Related: the loop and its signals in [15 learning loop](15-learning-loop.md); the behaviour oracle in [16 behaviour oracle](16-behaviour-oracle.md); the method adoption and validators in [17 engine2](17-engine2-validators-and-method.md); the service modules in [23 build service](23-build-service.md).

## What is and is not "training"
| Thing | Is it model training? | What it actually is |
|---|---|---|
| Version API sheets, failure rules, prompt text | No | Text injected into the prompt / checked after generation. Changing it needs an image bump and an eval. |
| Starter bank (16 prebuilt mods) | No | Hand-built, tested mods served with zero model calls on an exact template match. |
| Recipe memory (10 patterns) | No | Verified mechanic patterns added to the FIRST user turn (system prompt unchanged, so the cache prefix stays warm), with a 20% A/B holdback. |
| Learning loop (signals, mining) | No | Anonymised outcome counts -> **candidates** a person reviews. Nothing is auto-applied (D-61). |
| Distillation (S0-S3) | No | A one-time extraction of FACTS (event names, method traps, version differences) from a private reference corpus into sheets, rules and goldens. No third-party code or text is copied. |
| Eval harness | No | Measures the above; gates a release. |
| Customer data | Not used to train anything | Outcome data only, anonymised, D-60 ([15](15-learning-loop.md)); template sharing is a separate opt-in. |
| Anthropic's own models | Not ours | Cyrus has no influence on them; the Terms disclose that prompts are processed by Anthropic ([06 portals](06-portals.md) legal section). |

## The knowledge stack (where each piece lives)
| Layer | Source of truth | Size today (repo) | Verified by | Changed through |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **API sheets** per version | `services/modbuilder/sheets/<version>.md`, `api-facts.json` -> `api-facts.verified.json` | 4 versions (1.21.1, 1.21.4, 1.21.8, 1.21.11), about 9-10k tokens each | `sheets/verify-api-facts.py` runs `javap` on the resolved Paper classpaths on node-2; `gen-sheets.py` renders only facts that version's jar has | edit facts, re-verify, regenerate, image bump |
| **Failure rules** | `services/modbuilder/rules/failure-rules.json` | 55 rules, version `rules-2026-10-13.1` | `precheck.js` patterns + goldens; each rule cites a source | new rule = diff + test + image bump |
| **Network policy** | `rules/net-policy.json` | host allow-list, rates | scanner + tests | owner-reviewed |
| **Prompts** | `services/modbuilder/prompts.js` | `mb-2026-10-14.1` (+ techniques prompt `mb-tech-2026-10-12.2`) | eval gate (a prompt change moves quality) | normal branch; recorded in the release record |
| **Golden plugins** | `services/modbuilder/golden/plugins/**` | 77 | `golden/harness.js` compiles + scans every one on every version; Test Flight boots the flown ones; `results.json` feeds [minecraft-coverage.md](minecraft-coverage.md) | add a golden with every technique |
| **Starter bank** | `services/modbuilder/bank/**` | 16 | compile + scan on 4 versions, real Test Flight 1.21.11 and 1.21.4: 16/16 enabled, 28/28 RCON checks (tracker 102) | `MB_STARTER_BANK` (service) + `CYRUS_STARTER_BANK` (portal) |
| **Recipe memory** | `services/modbuilder/recipes/*.json` | 10 | holdback A/B measured by path memory | `MB_RECIPES`, `MB_RECIPES_HOLDBACK_PCT` |
| **Coverage archetypes** | `lib/cyrus/adapters/minecraft-coverage.json` -> `minecraft-coverage.md` | about 70-85 archetypes | coverage eval top-1 >= 90% test | edit JSON, run `scripts/cyrus/mc-coverage.ts` |
| **Coach templates** | `lib/cyrus/coach/**` | one per archetype | tests | `CYRUS_PROMPT_COACH` |
| **Paper member index** | built at image time by `tools/gen-member-index.js` | per version | did-you-mean: 0 wrong rewrites on about 8,500 mutations (CE) | `MB_MEMBER_INDEX` |
| **Spyglass data** | `spyglass-data.json` sha256 pins (6 versions) | offline at image build | pinned hashes | `MB_SPYGLASS` |
| **Reference corpus** | private, outside git (`/tank/cyrus-library-staging/_reference-mods`, `/tank/cyrus-knowledge`) | 386 items | aggregate facts only | never published |
| **Universal-modder skills** | `docs/third-party/universal-modder` (vendored, MIT) + inventory `docs/cyrus/onboarding/skills/README.md`; the 74-game field-note KB is private | 11 skills | research input only | reuse-before-research for new games ([27](27-games.md)) |

Distillation S0-S3 (2026-10-13, report BN): inventory of the 386-item corpus (173 plugins, 141 data packs, 43 resource packs, 29 other-loader), 68 new javap-verified event/method facts (sheets +about 800 tokens each), rules from usage frequency, 12 more goldens. The corpus text and code never entered git, prompts or goldens (GPL / AGPL / ARR material was never copied or paraphrased).

## The loop that improves it (human in the loop)
```
real builds --> signals (rework, retry, regression, guard refusal, flight failure, cost) --> report + mining
    --> CANDIDATES (failure-rule | sheet-fact | golden-case | routing-rule | prompt-coach-gap)
    --> review queue (admin Learning tab, nothing auto-applied) --> normal branch with tests
    --> eval gate vs the accepted baseline --> engine release manifest --> image bump (owner)
```
- Code: `lib/cyrus/learning/**`, `scripts/cyrus/learning-report.ts`, `learning-mine.ts`; flag `CYRUS_LEARNING` (ON in the portal env as of 2026-10-15).
- A **path memory** keeps which prompt shape went down which path (tier, effort, bank / recipe / plain) and what it cost, derived ids only.
- The first token-efficiency baseline (27 owner builds, $6.51) and the expected impact estimates are in [15](15-learning-loop.md); estimates stay labelled ESTIMATE until the holdback measures them.

## The eval harness
`scripts/cyrus/eval-run.ts` drives real builds through the real portal path (or the service) and journals everything under `/root/cyrus-eval/<tag>/` (outside git). Code: `lib/cyrus/eval/**`, corpora in `services/modbuilder/eval/`.
| Piece | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Presets** | `first-run` (90 builds across lanes, coverage and techniques), `coverage-first` (42 builds, per version), `real-world` (80 messy owner-style prompts, strata creature 30% / GUI-economy-quests 25% / items 20% / datapack-world 10% / admin-minigames 15%; about $14-31, mid $22.6) and `real-world-smoke` (24 prompts; always with `--testflight`) |
| **Stages reported separately** | compiled, scanned, booted, plugin enabled, commands registered, assets delivered, portal sync, behaviour (oracle) |
| **Real pass** | built AND plugin enabled in the Test Flight AND every planned lane shipped AND portal sync not failing AND behaviour not failed. "Not flown" is never a pass (`lib/cyrus/eval/realpass.ts`) |
| **pass@1** | real pass with no model repair |
| **Failure taxonomy** | one primary class per non-pass (timeout, budget, false refusal, perf guard, compile, scan, missing depend, did not enable, design downgrade ...), ranked (`lib/cyrus/eval/taxonomy.ts`) |
| **Oracle** | `--oracle` adds the behaviour stage ([16](16-behaviour-oracle.md)) |
| **Gate** | `scripts/cyrus/eval-gate.ts`: a 20-prompt verdict vs the accepted baseline; a pass-rate drop of more than 1 point blocks; `real regressions` only when both sides carry real pass; recorded per image tag; weekly timer `cyrus-eval-gate.timer` (needs `CYRUS_EVAL_GATE_BUDGET_USD`) |
| **Baseline** | `services/modbuilder/eval/baseline.json` + `gate-accepted.json` are written ONLY by an owner-reviewed accept commit. **Neither file exists in the repo today**, so the gate verdict is `no-reference` (WARN) |
| **Stats** | `scripts/cyrus/eval-journal-stats.ts <dir> --compare <dir>` |

### Measured history (journals are outside git; reports in `/root/claudeskills/agent-notes/cyrus-research/`)
| Run | Image | Builds | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| first1 (2026-10-13) | 0.11 | 59 of 90, $19.56 | final pass 98.3%, pass@1 57.6%, real boot 100% (58/58); 42% of builds needed repairs = 65% of spend |
| second1 (2026-10-13) | 0.13 | 38 | pass@1 48% -> 86% on the 37 identical prompts; repair share of spend 76% -> 23%; average cost $0.37 -> $0.30 |
| fourth1 (2026-10-14) | 0.16 | 70 of 90 read | pass@1 75.7%; texture 11/21, designer 11/15 |
| fourth1 re-scored with real pass | - | - | real pass 97.8% (BZ) |
| fifth1 re-scored offline | - | - | old pass@1 100% but REAL pass 79.2% (4 designer downgrades + 1 texture check) |
| rc11 replay (estimate, not measured) | - | - | pass@1 75.7% -> 84.3% (rc10) -> 97.1% (rc10 + rc11) |
Honest limits: every eval ran on the subscription login; no run exists for images 0.17 onward; the real-world preset has never been run with spend ("No paid eval run", BZ).

## Verification ladder (what "tested" means)
`static` (compiled and checked) < `synthetic` (MockBukkit pre-flight) < `booted` (real Test Flight) < `behaviour` (oracle / playtest on a real server) < `client` (a real Minecraft client; **nothing records this yet**) (`lib/cyrus/evidence/levels.ts`). The studio shows the rung reached; a skipped rung never counts.

## Rules for changing the knowledge
1. Facts first: verify with `javap` on every buildable version before a sheet or rule says it.
2. A rule has a pattern, versions, a fix and a source; prefer a deterministic autofix over a prompt sentence.
3. Every prompt-token addition is measured (sheets +800 tokens per version was accepted; the boss-model line is about 126 tokens).
4. Proof = unit test + golden + (for runtime claims) a real Test Flight record in `agent-notes/cyrus-research/*flights*.json`.
5. Never put third-party code, licence-restricted text or the owner's game archives into sheets, rules, goldens or docs.
6. Record the change in the release manifest and [11 history](11-history.md); update `doc-owners.json` if a new path appears.

# 26 Assets: the whole picture and the taxonomy

Everything Cyrus can use or ship that is not Java: models, textures, sounds, motion, HDRIs, sprites, packs, and the user's own files. The detailed rules and history are in [04 assets and library](04-assets-and-library.md) and [03 studios](03-studios.md); this page is the **map and the taxonomy**: how assets are classified, how they enter, how they are served, what is allowed to leave, and what is deliberately never public.

## Five questions every asset answers
1. **What is it?** a `kind` (what it physically is) plus a `category` (what it is for) plus tags and style.
2. **Where did it come from?** provenance `source` (`user`, `ai`, `library`, `import`, `template`) and `derivedFrom`.
3. **May we keep / share / ship it?** its legal **class** and licence **tier**.
4. **Is it good enough?** measured descriptors and the quality gates.
5. **Where do the bytes live?** staging (read only), content-addressed store (derivatives), pack host, or the build job's workspace only.

## Legal classes (the gate; `lib/cyrus/assets3d/ledger.ts`, `lib/cyrus/gameassets/policy.ts`)
| Class | Meaning | Kept beyond the job | Library | Redistribute | Deliverable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `user-original` | authored in a studio | yes | yes | yes | full |
| `ai-generated-for-user` | made by Cyrus for the user | yes | yes | yes | full |
| `platform-library` | Nxeon-owned or CC0 | yes | yes | yes | full |
| `third-party-licensed` | uploaded under someone else's licence | yes | **no** | no | full |
| `game-derived` | derived from a game's own files | **no** | **no** | **no** | delta-only |
Rule: **game-derived never outlives its job, never enters a library, never ships.** Only content authored inside Cyrus with an empty `derivedFrom` is even eligible for contribution; eligible is not published (content filters and the Terms grant still gate).

## Licence tiers in the catalogue (`lib/cyrus/library/v2/entry.ts`)
`cc0`, `cc-by`, `proprietary-nxeon`, `user-contributed`. The community library is **CC0-only, no creator credit** (owner decision), so CC-BY rows are excluded (4,132 rows kept aside), as are sources with new no-redistribution licences, Mixamo/CMU, CC-BY-NC and Sampling+ clips. The owner's proprietary SFX (2,964 files; licensor terms: modify and use in games allowed, distributing the files alone or in a bundle prohibited) is heard by customers only through processed in-game use after the owner clears it (`CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED`); raw audio is never served. Per-source licence evidence: `LICENCE-LEDGER.csv` (about 670 rows) and `_lic/` in staging (private, outside git).

## Kinds (`CATALOG_KINDS`)
| Group | Kinds | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 3D and surface | `model`, `texture-set` (PBR), `texture`, `sprite`, `hdri`, `decal` | plan gate: visual assets are the top plan ("All models") |
| Audio | `sound`, `music` | audio gated by Saka and above; proprietary bank only when cleared |
| Motion and effects | `flipbook`, `particle-texture`, `animation-clip`, `animated-model`, `motion-preset`, `effect-preset` | MotionSpec JSON for presets |
Reference-only rows (`v:item:...`, status `reference`, game-derived) describe vanilla items by id and are never servable or contributable (`CYRUS_VANILLA_CATALOG`).

## Category taxonomy (vocabulary v1: `lib/cyrus/library/v2/vocab.json`, 132 category ids)
Ids are `<domain>/<sub>`. `sound/*` reuses `lib/cyrus/sound/taxonomy.json` and `pixel/*` reuses `lib/cyrus/texture-library/taxonomy.json`.
| Domain | Subcategories |
|---|---|
| `weapons` | melee, ranged, firearms, explosives, ammo, shields |
| `architecture` | walls-floors, buildings, doors-windows, stairs-bridges, roofs, fences, ruins |
| `nature` | trees, rocks, foliage, terrain |
| `props` | containers, tools, hardware, lights, signs, debris, street, treasure, books, misc |
| `furniture` | seating, tables, storage, beds, decor, lighting |
| `decor` | signs-plaques, monuments-statues, vases-pots |
| `characters` / `creatures` | humanoids, base-meshes / animals, monsters, insects, dinosaurs |
| `vehicles` | ground, air-space, water, rail, military |
| `food`, `household`, `toys`, `music`, `scifi` | meals, produce, drinks / kitchenware, electronics, bathroom, clothing, appliances / play, sports, tabletop, arcade / instruments, score, ambient-drone / tech |
| `ui`, `sprites`, `tiles`, `items` | buttons-panels, icons, cursors-crosshairs, input-prompts, cards-board, fonts / general / tilesets / collectibles |
| `vfx` | particles, fire, smoke, explosion, water, sparks, muzzle-flash, impact, magic, electric, slash, dust, weather, liquid-loop |
| `material` | metal, wood, stone, brick, tiles, marble, concrete, ground, fabric, plastic-rubber, glass, facade-roofing, organic, scifi-panel, pattern, atlas |
| `env` | day-sky, sunset-dawn, night, overcast, indoor, outdoor |
| `sound` | weapons, doors_mechanisms, creatures_voices, crowd_reactions, music_stingers, impacts_destruction, movement, ui_alerts, magic_energy, environment_ambience, vehicle... |
| `pixel` | items, blocks, entity_skins, gui, particles |
| `motion` | creature-clip, humanoid-clip, weapon-clip, mechanism-clip, vehicle-clip, clip |
| `misc` | uncategorised |
Other vocabulary: 12 styles (low-poly, stylised, realistic, pixel-art, voxel, hand-painted, toon, one-bit, sketch, photoscan, flat, isometric); tag facets (theme, material, color, condition, tech, sound, motion-effect, clip verb, blend hint, playback, view, size); 103 `useFor` situations (for example "gunshot sound", "melee swing sound", "explosion effect") that the planner and `catalog_search` use to pick an asset for a purpose; real-world scale hints for models; source style hints (Kenney, Quaternius, KayKit, Poly Haven, ambientCG). Each entry carries one primary and up to 3 secondary categories, up to 8 free tags and measured descriptors (audio duration / intensity / pitch band / loopable; texture size / palette / transparency / tileable / style).

## Pipeline: ingest to served
```
source packs (read only)  /tank/cyrus-library-staging/<source>/...
   -> licence gate (ledger + CC0 evidence + path hygiene)  [lib/cyrus/library/backend/licence-gate.ts]
   -> catalog v2 entries, id cat:<sha256>      stage A (no AI: path/filename/descriptors)  [lib/cyrus/library/v2/stage-a.ts]
                                               stage B/C (optional AI tagging, owner tier + cap)  [stage-b.ts, stage-c.ts]
   -> dedupe (image dhash, audio envelope, glb facts, motion JSON)  [dedupe.ts]
   -> import to Postgres: CyrusCatalogEntry + CyrusCatalogTerm (posting lists)  [scripts/cyrus/library-import-prod.ts]
   -> lazy deterministic derivatives (thumb, preview-ogg, glb-opt, bundle) in the content-addressed store
   -> signed 5-minute viewer-scoped URLs (raw audio never; proprietary only when cleared)
   -> studios browse / "Use in project" / catalog tools inside builds / library API v1
contribution (customer-made, automatic, CC0): filters + hold queue -> published | held -> removed (takedown)
```
- Backend: content-addressed object store (local or S3, caps, 30-day retention); admin pages `/admin/cyrus/library/*` (hold queue, near duplicates, contribution settings, takedown).
- **Production load (2026-10-14, report CC):** 62,777 staged entries and 1,145,478 postings rehearsed on a throwaway database in 63 s; the licence gate refused 0 of the staged file; 62,444 published, 43 held, 290 removed in the staged file; 56.5% fully described. Five serving bugs found by validating through the real handlers were fixed (long-audio previews, audio over 48 MB, glob flipbooks and ambientCG model folders, Poly Haven sets, `.hdr` thumbnails). One paste does it: `scripts/cyrus/library-prod-apply.sh plan|apply|rollback`. As of 2026-10-15 the portal env carries `CYRUS_LIBRARY_BACKEND=1`, `CYRUS_LIBRARY_BROWSE=1` and `CYRUS_LIBRARY_CONTRIBUTE=1` (names read from the env file; the row count in the live database was **not** re-measured here: run `scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh` or look at `/admin/cyrus/library`).
- Known gaps: `glb-opt@1` needs gltf-transform (original served); about 780 assets have no image to thumbnail; animation clips have no variant of their own; trademark filter list is a stub until the owner supplies one; filters are text-only (no pixel or audio classifier).

## Quality gates by lane (what must be true before an asset ships)
| Lane | Gate | Code |
|---|---|---|
| texture | palette / size rules, solid-panel inset fix, `vanilla_lookalike` against private fingerprints when present | `lib/cyrus/textures/**`, `services/modbuilder/textures.js` |
| sound | layers <= 4 (thinning), loudness / peak checks after render, rubric fix | `lib/cyrus/sound/**`, `services/modbuilder/sounds.js` |
| model | glTF <= 32 MiB, 150k triangles, layer budget, perf budget | `lib/cyrus/modelstudio/**` |
| any pack | `pack-check`, content-addressed names, Pack Loader hand-off, Spyglass (optional) | `lib/cyrus/versions/vanilla/**`, `services/modbuilder/spyglass.js` |
| asset-quality eval | 16 prompts with a rubric (BP) | `services/modbuilder/eval/` |

## Bring-your-own game assets and the vanilla index
The owner's Minecraft archives and any user's own game files are **game-derived**: private reference only. Distilled facts (ids, paths, sizes, numbers; no pixels, audio or geometry) are in `lib/cyrus/versions/vanilla/26.1.2/*.json` and `docs/cyrus/asset-index.json`; the raw index is outside git and read only when `CYRUS_VANILLA_REFERENCE_DIR` is set (otherwise every check says "not run" and BYO is refused). `CYRUS_BYO_GAME_ASSETS=1` is ON in the portal env as of 2026-10-15: the studios' game tab reads the user's own files in the browser, sends hashes only, re-hashes server side, stamps `legalClass: game-derived`, deletes after 7 days and ships delta-only. Never put the archives' contents in these docs.

## Operational facts
- Staging volume (not served, not in git): about 139 GB library files + 46 GB incoming; SFX 51 GB; backed up by the nightly job and the Dropbox restic repo ([21 infrastructure](21-infrastructure.md)).
- Storage quotas per plan for customer files (`CYRUS_STORAGE`, ON): Free 1 GB (PLACEHOLDER), Katara 5, Saka 25, Yakko 50 GB ([29 decisions](29-decisions-and-placeholders.md)).
- Takedown: a legal report or three reporters hold an asset; takedown removes now, purges derivatives, marks dependents; mods already built keep their copy (current rule, owner decision open).

The community library is **CC0-only, no creator credit** (owner decision), so CC-BY rows are excluded (4,132 rows kept aside), as are sources with new no-redistribution licences, Mixamo/CMU, CC-BY-NC and Sampling+ clips. The owner's proprietary SFX (2,964 files; licensor terms: modify and use in games allowed, distributing the files alone or in a bundle prohibited) is heard by customers only through processed in-game use after the owner clears it (`CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED`); raw audio is never served. Per-source licence evidence: `LICENCE-LEDGER.csv` (about 670 rows) and `_lic/` in staging (private, outside git).

## Kinds (`CATALOG_KINDS`)
| Group | Kinds | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 3D and surface | `model`, `texture-set` (PBR), `texture`, `sprite`, `hdri`, `decal` | plan gate: visual assets are the top plan ("All models") |
| Audio | `sound`, `music` | audio gated by Saka and above; proprietary bank only when cleared |
| Motion and effects | `flipbook`, `particle-texture`, `animation-clip`, `animated-model`, `motion-preset`, `effect-preset` | MotionSpec JSON for presets |
Reference-only rows (`v:item:...`, status `reference`, game-derived) describe vanilla items by id and are never servable or contributable (`CYRUS_VANILLA_CATALOG`).

## Category taxonomy (vocabulary v1: `lib/cyrus/library/v2/vocab.json`, 132 category ids)
Ids are `<domain>/<sub>`. `sound/*` reuses `lib/cyrus/sound/taxonomy.json` and `pixel/*` reuses `lib/cyrus/texture-library/taxonomy.json`.
| Domain | Subcategories |

| `architecture` | walls-floors, buildings, doors-windows, stairs-bridges, roofs, fences, ruins |

Other vocabulary: 12 styles (low-poly, stylised, realistic, pixel-art, voxel, hand-painted, toon, one-bit, sketch, photoscan, flat, isometric); tag facets (theme, material, color, condition, tech, sound, motion-effect, clip verb, blend hint, playback, view, size); 103 `useFor` situations (for example "gunshot sound", "melee swing sound", "explosion effect") that the planner and `catalog_search` use to pick an asset for a purpose; real-world scale hints for models; source style hints (Kenney, Quaternius, KayKit, Poly Haven, ambientCG). Each entry carries one primary and up to 3 secondary categories, up to 8 free tags and measured descriptors (audio duration / intensity / pitch band / loopable; texture size / palette / transparency / tileable / style).

## Pipeline: ingest to served
```
source packs (read only)  /tank/cyrus-library-staging/<source>/...
   -> licence gate (ledger + CC0 evidence + path hygiene)  [lib/cyrus/library/backend/licence-gate.ts]
   -> catalog v2 entries, id cat:<sha256>      stage A (no AI: path/filename/descriptors)  [lib/cyrus/library/v2/stage-a.ts]
                                               stage B/C (optional AI tagging, owner tier + cap)  [stage-b.ts, stage-c.ts]
   -> dedupe (image dhash, audio envelope, glb facts, motion JSON)  [dedupe.ts]
   -> import to Postgres: CyrusCatalogEntry + CyrusCatalogTerm (posting lists)  [scripts/cyrus/library-import-prod.ts]
   -> lazy deterministic derivatives (thumb, preview-ogg, glb-opt, bundle) in the content-addressed store
   -> signed 5-minute viewer-scoped URLs (raw audio never; proprietary only when cleared)
   -> studios browse / "Use in project" / catalog tools inside builds / library API v1
contribution (customer-made, automatic, CC0): filters + hold queue -> published | held -> removed (takedown)
```
- Backend: content-addressed object store (local or S3, caps, 30-day retention); admin pages `/admin/cyrus/library/*` (hold queue, near duplicates, contribution settings, takedown).
- **Production load (2026-10-14, report CC):** 62,777 staged entries and 1,145,478 postings rehearsed on a throwaway database in 63 s; the licence gate refused 0 of the staged file; 62,444 published, 43 held, 290 removed in the staged file; 56.5% fully described. Five serving bugs found by validating through the real handlers were fixed (long-audio previews, audio over 48 MB, glob flipbooks and ambientCG model folders, Poly Haven sets, `.hdr` thumbnails). One paste does it: `scripts/cyrus/library-prod-apply.sh plan|apply|rollback`. As of 2026-10-15 the portal env carries `CYRUS_LIBRARY_BACKEND=1`, `CYRUS_LIBRARY_BROWSE=1` and `CYRUS_LIBRARY_CONTRIBUTE=1` (names read from the env file; the row count in the live database was **not** re-measured here: run `scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh` or look at `/admin/cyrus/library`).
- Known gaps: `glb-opt@1` needs gltf-transform (original served); about 780 assets have no image to thumbnail; animation clips have no variant of their own; trademark filter list is a stub until the owner supplies one; filters are text-only (no pixel or audio classifier).

## Quality gates by lane (what must be true before an asset ships)
| Lane | Gate | Code |
|---|---|---|
| texture | palette / size rules, solid-panel inset fix, `vanilla_lookalike` against private fingerprints when present | `lib/cyrus/textures/**`, `services/modbuilder/textures.js` |
| sound | layers <= 4 (thinning), loudness / peak checks after render, rubric fix | `lib/cyrus/sound/**`, `services/modbuilder/sounds.js` |
| model | glTF <= 32 MiB, 150k triangles, layer budget, perf budget | `lib/cyrus/modelstudio/**` |
| any pack | `pack-check`, content-addressed names, Pack Loader hand-off, Spyglass (optional) | `lib/cyrus/versions/vanilla/**`, `services/modbuilder/spyglass.js` |
| asset-quality eval | 16 prompts with a rubric (BP) | `services/modbuilder/eval/` |

## Bring-your-own game assets and the vanilla index
The owner's Minecraft archives and any user's own game files are **game-derived**: private reference only. Distilled facts (ids, paths, sizes, numbers; no pixels, audio or geometry) are in `lib/cyrus/versions/vanilla/26.1.2/*.json` and `docs/cyrus/asset-index.json`; the raw index is outside git and read only when `CYRUS_VANILLA_REFERENCE_DIR` is set (otherwise every check says "not run" and BYO is refused). `CYRUS_BYO_GAME_ASSETS=1` is ON in the portal env as of 2026-10-15: the studios' game tab reads the user's own files in the browser, sends hashes only, re-hashes server side, stamps `legalClass: game-derived`, deletes after 7 days and ships delta-only. Never put the archives' contents in these docs.

## Operational facts
- Staging volume (not served, not in git): about 139 GB library files + 46 GB incoming; SFX 51 GB; backed up by the nightly job and the Dropbox restic repo ([21 infrastructure](21-infrastructure.md)).
- Storage quotas per plan for customer files (`CYRUS_STORAGE`, ON): Free 1 GB (PLACEHOLDER), Katara 5, Saka 25, Yakko 50 GB ([29 decisions](29-decisions-and-placeholders.md)).
- Takedown: a legal report or three reporters hold an asset; takedown removes now, purges derivatives, marks dependents; mods already built keep their copy (current rule, owner decision open).

## Part 1: How Rust modding works (one page, also usable on the marketing page)

**A Rust mod is a server plugin.** It's one C# source file (`MyPlugin.cs`). The server compiles it, so you don't build it first. Two frameworks run these plugins:

- **Oxide (uMod).** The long-standing standard, MIT open source. It ships patched copies of the game's server DLLs. Plugins live in `oxide/plugins`, settings in `oxide/config`, saved data in `oxide/data`, translations in `oxide/lang`, logs in `oxide/logs`.
- **Carbon.** A newer framework that runs the same Oxide plugins unchanged. Instead of shipping patched DLLs it patches the game at runtime, and it uses `carbon/plugins` and similar folders. Oxide and Carbon can't be installed on the same server. Nxeon offers Oxide today. Carbon 

**Install and reload.** Drop the `.cs` file into the plugins folder. Within seconds the framework compiles it (Roslyn, C# 14) and loads it. Edit the file and it hot-reloads. No restart, no downtime. On first load the plugin writes its own config file, and you edit that to tune it

**Players install nothing.** Rust has no client modding: the game client is protected by Easy Anti-Cheat and has no mod loader. Plugins still change a lot of what players experience:
- menus, HUDs and overlays (CUI, drawn by the server and sent to each player),
- chat commands and messages,
- custom versions of existing items (renamed, re-skinned with Steam Workshop skins, given new behaviour),
- spawned NPCs, vehicles, crates and events,
- gather rates, loot, crafting, raid rules and weather.

----
Nxeon runs Palworld on the **native Linux dedicated server only** (no Windows, no Wine/Proton). What Cyrus does:

| Request | What Cyrus does on Nxeon | Players install? |
|---|---|---|
| Server rules and balance: XP, capture, day/night length, pal and player damage, hunger, stamina, drops, gathering, work speed, egg hatch time, item weight, death penalty, PvP, hardcore, raids, fast travel, base and guild limits, randomizer, performance limits | **Builds a serve
| Visual / interface tips: pal stats overlay, colour grade | **Builds a client-side tip**, labelled "client-side only: your own Windows PC, not your server" | Only the player who wants it |
| Anything needing a server script (spawn tables, rare variants, weapon retunes, base-job loops) | **Refuses**, says why (Palworld only loads server scripts on Windows), and offers the closest settings preset where an honest one exists (spawns -> spawn/drop rates, weapon -> playe
| Single-player / co-op-host scripts (spells, loot satchel, companion, expeditions, quests) and both-sides scripts (mount speed) | **Refuses**: the game ignores them on a dedicated server | n/a |
| New textures, models, sounds, Blueprint mods | **Refuses**: need cooked Unreal 5.1 packages on every player's PC | n/a |

The generator can still produce the other Lua kinds (`palworldLuaPackage`) and the validator lints them with
`{ nxeon: false }`, so nothing is lost if the policy ever changes, but `buildModFiles` (what customers get) never ships them.
Palworld must not be marked live on the strength of Windows-only mods; what is ready to consider is the settings preset path.

## Verdict: Linux vs Windows (confirmed from primary sources)

**Confirmed.** Pocketpair's own server guide says server-side mods work only on the **Windows** dedicated server

# 27 Games: what is live, what is ready, how a game is onboarded

Cyrus is a game-agnostic core with one game built for real: **Minecraft (Paper / Purpur server plugins)**. Every other game exists as research, a generator and validators, an honest readiness checklist, and a registry row with status `soon`. Flipping a game to `live` is the owner's decision. Generated detail: [reference/adapters.md](reference/adapters.md) (registry, capability matrix) and [reference/versions.md](reference/versions.md) (version registry). Per-game checklists: [readiness/](readiness/valheim.md). The repeatable procedure: [onboarding/PLAYBOOK.md](onboarding/PLAYBOOK.md).

## Status board (2026-10-15)
| Game | Registry id | Registry status | Adapter (`ADAPTERS`) | What exists | Not done / blocked |

## Platform hardening after the 2026-10-15 scraper incident (branch `feature/nx-hardening`, NOT deployed)

**Incident (2026-10-15 ~04:50 UTC).** A distributed scraper (many IPs, rotating user agents) walked `/mods?sort=latest&page=8000+`.
Deep OFFSET pagination makes Postgres sort and skip tens of thousands of rows per request; hundreds of multi-minute SELECTs ran at once
(web 77% CPU, load 25 on 8 threads, swap full) while vzdump, a Cyrus SFX rsync and a Dropbox sync also ran. One nginx line
(`return 444` for `/mods` with `page>=100`) restored service. This branch makes the app, the DB role, the schedule and the alerts
survive a repeat without that manual line.

### Change history (this branch)
- **2026-10-15 - public list routes cannot be walked deep (app layer).** `lib/list-guard.ts` (pure, edge-safe) + `middleware.ts`: any
  GET/HEAD to a non-authenticated path with `page` > `NXEON_MAX_PUBLIC_PAGE` (default 100) or `offset|skip|start` > 2,500 is answered 404
  from middleware with no page code or DB work (repeat params like `page=2&page=99999` and `1e9`/`Infinity` are handled); list-shaped
  URLs (a query string with page/q/sort/category/loader/version/...) are limited per IP to `NXEON_LIST_RATE_MAX` (default 90) per minute,
  answered 429 + `Retry-After`. `/admin`, `/staff`, `/dashboard`, `/api`, `/_next` and static files are not touched.
  Defence in depth: `queryCatalogMods` (the single catalogue query behind `/mods`, `/mods/games/<family>`, NxLabs) clamps `page` to the cap

# 28 Operations handbook

The practical, ordered "what do I do" page for whoever runs Cyrus: daily and weekly checks, how to deploy and roll back each artifact, incident response, capacity. It is a front door to the authoritative step lists: [CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK](../CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK.md) (owner, step by step), [LAUNCH-RUNBOOK](LAUNCH-RUNBOOK.md) (launch, watch, break-glass), [07 operations](07-operations.md) (detail and history) and [21 infrastructure](21-infrastructure.md) (the map). Nothing here is executed by an agent: the owner (or the operator he names) runs every production step. Agents work in worktrees on node-2 only ([14 how to work here](14-how-to-work-here.md)).

## The one command that tells you where you are
```
scripts/cyrus/launch-check.sh [beta|public]        # read only; PASS / WARN / FAIL per check, GO / NO-GO, with the fix
scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh [all|migrations|service|worker|flags|packs|delivery|storage|launch]
```
The hourly `cyrus-launch-check.timer` writes the same data for the admin **Launch check** tab. Do not take a step marked "requires GO" while it says NO-GO.

## Daily (5 minutes)
| Check | Where | Healthy | If not |
|---|---|---|---|
| Launch check summary | admin Launch tab or `launch-check.sh beta` | no FAIL beyond the known owner-only items | open the named check; fix list is printed |
| Build service up and sane | `GET <tunnel>/health` or admin Live | `auth` as expected, `capacity` not breaker-open, queue shallow | restart is the owner's call; see "Build service" below |
| Queue and waits | admin Live: Build capacity panel | queue < 6 waiting (`cyrus_capacity_alert_queue_depth`), p80 wait under the alert minutes | check the AI breaker (session limit), then `MB_CONCURRENCY` |
| Failures | admin Builds, filter failed | no new error class | read the release record (flight verdict, errors); our-side failures are free for the customer |
| Spend | admin Cost, alert `ai-spend-24h` | under `CYRUS_SPEND_ALERT_USD` | find the account (BQ ceilings cap planner/coach abuse) |
| Backups | `launch-check` backup-fresh; marker `CYRUS_OFFBOX_STATUS` | newer than 36 h | see "Backups" below |
| Disk (root) | alert `disk-primary-root` | below the threshold; the primary root was 87% on 2026-10-15 | clear only known-safe caches ([07 operations](07-operations.md) incident table); never write build output to root |
| Alerts reaching a human | Discord webhook | set | **not set as of 2026-10-15**: alerts only print to the journal until `CYRUS_ALERT_DISCORD_WEBHOOK` is set |

## Weekly
- Eval gate verdict (`cyrus-eval-gate.timer`, Sunday 04:30; needs `CYRUS_EVAL_GATE_BUDGET_USD`; it spends money) and the baseline acceptance procedure ([07 operations](07-operations.md) "Eval baseline acceptance"). **No accepted baseline exists yet**, so the gate says `no-reference`.
- Restore drill result (Monday 07:30 Dropbox drill); quarterly the full scenario table in [07 operations](07-operations.md) "Backups and restore".
- Learning report and candidates (`scripts/cyrus/learning-report.ts`, admin Learning tab): review, never auto-apply ([15](15-learning-loop.md)).
- Storage report and quota breaches (admin Storage), library hold queue and takedown reports (`/admin/cyrus/library/*`).
- TLS expiry for cyrus.my (alert rules `cert-cyrus-my`, `cert-cyrus-my-origin`).
- Open PRs and branches vs main: [20 coverage matrix](20-coverage-matrix.md) "Status snapshot"; run `git branch --no-merged main | grep cyrus`.
- Rotations pending from earlier incidents: Cloudflare token pasted in chat, Dropbox token, any key that was ever in a journal (alert errors once printed the DB URL: now redacted).

## Deploy (owner runs; one at a time; smoke after each)
Hazards first: never build or edit in `/opt/nxeon` (raw `npm run build` + restart caused two outages on 2026-10-01); check `uptime` (a promote on an overloaded primary rolls itself back); never `pkill -f`; never `git add -A`; new SQL is additive and run by hand.
| Artifact | Steps | Check | Rollback |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Portal** | `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>`, look at it, `scripts/promote-production.sh` (after stopping staging: `--skip-staging-check`) | `/api/cyrus/health` names the release commit; launch-check; `smoke-readonly.sh all` | automatic if the new release fails smoke; later `scripts/rollback-release.sh --production [RELEASE_ID]` (does not roll back the worker or schema) |
| **Database** | manual additive SQL in `prisma/manual-migrations/*cyrus*.sql` (list in [reference/db-tables.md](reference/db-tables.md)); then `smoke-readonly.sh migrations` | tables present | additive, so old code keeps working; `scripts/cyrus/rc-migration-rehearsal.sh` rehearses on a throwaway DB |
| **Build service image** | `TAG=modbuilder:<n> bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh` (service must be idle: not while an eval or a customer build runs) | health `promptVersion`, scanner and registry hashes, guard refusal | the script rolls back to the previous tag; manual: `run.sh <previous tag>` on the VM |
| **Image + API key** | `API_KEY=... deploy-modbuilder.sh` then `/health auth=api_key` | required before ANY public launch | re-run with the subscription login only for private work |
| **Flags and settings** | admin Flags tab (typed confirmations `LAUNCH CYRUS` / `CLOSE CYRUS` for the launch pair); env flags need an env edit and a web restart | the Flags page "since" history | settings are read per request: set back; kill switches in the Flags tab |
| **Landing (cyrus.my)** | `apps/cyrus-site/publish.sh` (dry run unless `--go`) | status page, nginx matrix `scripts/cyrus/nginx-cyrus-my-check.sh` | release dir symlink swap |
| **Library production load** | `scripts/cyrus/library-prod-apply.sh plan`, then `apply` | row counts verified by the script; health auto env-rollback | `rollback` |
| **Backup staggering** | `deploy/backup/stagger/install.sh --dry-run` then install | `systemctl list-timers 'nxeon-*' 'cyrus-*'` | `install.sh --revert` |
Order for a normal release train: DB (if any) -> portal -> image (if services/modbuilder changed) -> flags. The portal must tolerate an old image (it checks `/health features`), so the order is safe either way.

## Incident response
1. **Stabilise first** (any of: 5xx, slow, DB saturated): `uptime`, `systemctl status nxeon-web nxeon-worker`, `journalctl -u nxeon-web -n 100`, nginx access log tail. Stop heavy jobs (backups, evals) before touching the app.
2. **Classify** using the table; each row names a prior incident and its fix:
| Symptom | First suspect | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Whole site 5xx, DB slow, load spikes, swap full | scraper walking list pages (2026-10-15) or overlapping backups | emergency nginx `return 444` for deep `page=`; app guard `lib/list-guard.ts` (branch `feature/nx-hardening`, merged to main, install the nginx and role steps from its report); stop `cyrus-backup` / vzdump overlap |
| Cyrus builds all fail "ai_unavailable" | subscription session limit shared with agents and evals | wait for the reset; switch to an API key (launch prerequisite) |
| Builds stuck at one line for minutes | silent model (not stuck); old service without progress feed | check `/health` `features.progress`; do not restart mid-build |

Nothing here is executed by an agent: the owner (or the operator he names) runs every production step. Agents work in worktrees on node-2 only ([14 how to work here](14-how-to-work-here.md)).

## The one command that tells you where you are
```
scripts/cyrus/launch-check.sh [beta|public]        # read only; PASS / WARN / FAIL per check, GO / NO-GO, with the fix
scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh [all|migrations|service|worker|flags|packs|delivery|storage|launch]
```
The hourly `cyrus-launch-check.timer` writes the same data for the admin **Launch check** tab. Do not take a step marked "requires GO" while it says NO-GO.

## Daily (5 minutes)
| Check | Where | Healthy | If not |
|---|---|---|---|
| Launch check summary | admin Launch tab or `launch-check.sh beta` | no FAIL beyond the known owner-only items | open the named check; fix list is printed |
| Build service up and sane | `GET <tunnel>/health` or admin Live | `auth` as expected, `capacity` not breaker-open, queue shallow | restart is the owner's call; see "Build service" below |
| Queue and waits | admin Live: Build capacity panel | queue < 6 waiting (`cyrus_capacity_alert_queue_depth`), p80 wait under the alert minutes | check the AI breaker (session limit), then `MB_CONCURRENCY` |
| Failures | admin Builds, filter failed | no new error class | read the release record (flight verdict, errors); our-side failures are free for the customer |
| Spend | admin Cost, alert `ai-spend-24h` | under `CYRUS_SPEND_ALERT_USD` | find the account (BQ ceilings cap planner/coach abuse) |
| Backups | `launch-check` backup-fresh; marker `CYRUS_OFFBOX_STATUS` | newer than 36 h | see "Backups" below |
| Disk (root) | alert `disk-primary-root` | below the threshold; the primary root was 87% on 2026-10-15 | clear only known-safe caches ([07 operations](07-operations.md) incident table); never write build output to root |
| Alerts reaching a human | Discord webhook | set | **not set as of 2026-10-15**: alerts only print to the journal until `CYRUS_ALERT_DISCORD_WEBHOOK` is set |

## Weekly
- Eval gate verdict (`cyrus-eval-gate.timer`, Sunday 04:30; needs `CYRUS_EVAL_GATE_BUDGET_USD`; it spends money) and the baseline acceptance procedure ([07 operations](07-operations.md) "Eval baseline acceptance"). **No accepted baseline exists yet**, so the gate says `no-reference`.
- Restore drill result (Monday 07:30 Dropbox drill); quarterly the full scenario table in [07 operations](07-operations.md) "Backups and restore".
- Learning report and candidates (`scripts/cyrus/learning-report.ts`, admin Learning tab): review, never auto-apply ([15](15-learning-loop.md)).
- Storage report and quota breaches (admin Storage), library hold queue and takedown reports (`/admin/cyrus/library/*`).
- TLS expiry for cyrus.my (alert rules `cert-cyrus-my`, `cert-cyrus-my-origin`).
- Open PRs and branches vs main: [20 coverage matrix](20-coverage-matrix.md) "Status snapshot"; run `git branch --no-merged main | grep cyrus`.
- Rotations pending from earlier incidents: Cloudflare token pasted in chat, Dropbox token, any key that was ever in a journal (alert errors once printed the DB URL: now redacted).

Hazards first: never build or edit in `/opt/nxeon` (raw `npm run build` + restart caused two outages on 2026-10-01); check `uptime` (a promote on an overloaded primary rolls itself back); never `pkill -f`; never `git add -A`; new SQL is additive and run by hand.
| Artifact | Steps | Check | Rollback |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Portal** | `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>`, look at it, `scripts/promote-production.sh` (after stopping staging: `--skip-staging-check`) | `/api/cyrus/health` names the release commit; launch-check; `smoke-readonly.sh all` | automatic if the new release fails smoke; later `scripts/rollback-release.sh --production [RELEASE_ID]` (does not roll back the worker or schema) |
| **Database** | manual additive SQL in `prisma/manual-migrations/*cyrus*.sql` (list in [reference/db-tables.md](reference/db-tables.md)); then `smoke-readonly.sh migrations` | tables present | additive, so old code keeps working; `scripts/cyrus/rc-migration-rehearsal.sh` rehearses on a throwaway DB |
| **Build service image** | `TAG=modbuilder:<n> bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh` (service must be idle: not while an eval or a customer build runs) | health `promptVersion`, scanner and registry hashes, guard refusal | the script rolls back to the previous tag; manual: `run.sh <previous tag>` on the VM |
| **Image + API key** | `API_KEY=... deploy-modbuilder.sh` then `/health auth=api_key` | required before ANY public launch | re-run with the subscription login only for private work |
| **Flags and settings** | admin Flags tab (typed confirmations `LAUNCH CYRUS` / `CLOSE CYRUS` for the launch pair); env flags need an env edit and a web restart | the Flags page "since" history | settings are read per request: set back; kill switches in the Flags tab |

## Today (inside Nxeon) vs the target
Today Cyrus uses Nxeon's sign-in, wallet, Stripe and game-server install path directly (through the host seam, [01 architecture](01-architecture.md)). The target (defaults from the full plan, 2026-10-11): **Nxeon is the identity provider and the only money system; Cyrus sells nothing itself**; per-server scoped grants, never SSH credentials; a separate Cyrus Postgres; Cyrus has its own admin; separate Cyrus Terms/Privacy (lawyer-reviewed before public launch). These are the working defaults agents r37-r40 built to 

## SSO and identity (r36)
One app serves both hosts. `lib/cyrus/bridge/{config,routing}.ts` + middleware: cyrus.my gets the Cyrus brand bar around the same `/dashboard/cyrus` pages; the customer-app tree is exposed as `/home`, `/new`, `/account`, `/projects[/<id>]`; portal pages hand off to Nxeon; everything else 404s. **Sign in with Nxeon** = redirect with an Ed25519 signed assertion (state/nonce bound to the starting browser, single-use jti, exact `redirect_uri`, 120 s), a stable **subject id (Nxeon user id; never email)**, verified email
Verified: two-origin e2e 46/46 with the mode on and 6/6 off (no studio on cyrus.my, no IdP, internal tree 404, spoofed marker ignored); own-flow security review (open redirect, login CSRF, replay, forged subject, header spoofing, impersonation leak, fixation, consent/logout CSRF). Not run: `next build`, a real browser, staging behind nginx.

## Wallet, tokens and plans
- **Unit and sources**: see [00 overview](00-overview.md). 1 token = $0.002 of measured AI cost (`cyrus_tok_tokens_per_usd=500`), Yakko x1.25, min 5 per build. Game-server purchase grants `clamp(round5(100 + 16 x monthly $), 150, 750)`; each paid renewal `clamp(round5(25 + 6 x monthly $), 40, 300)` (only for games Cyrus builds for); lots expire after 90 days; plans Katara $4.99 = 750/month, Saka $19.99 = 3,500, All models $49.99 = 10,000, stacking, each month's tokens last 3 months; top-ups $5-$100 at 120 tokens/$,
- **Ledger**: append-only, idempotent (`idemKey` UNIQUE), reserve -> settle -> release per build; tables `CyrusTokenAccount/Lot/Ledger/Reservation`, `CyrusPlan`; the only writer is `lib/cyrus/tokens/ledger.ts`. Our-side failures are free (3 per rolling 7 days). Daily caps (5,000 tokens; 1,000 for accounts under 7 days). Sweep every 5 minutes.
- **Stripe**: plan prices found by lookup key `cyrus_plan_<tier>_v1` (`scripts/cyrus-tokens-stripe-setup.ts`, TEST mode; refuses a live key without an explicit override). Cyrus checkout sessions carry `cyrusUserId`, never the Nxeon user id, so Nxeon's wallet engine can never treat them as a top-up (pinned by a test).
- **Starter grant**: ONE free build (`cyrus_tok_starter=70`), with a guard against split launch flags.
- **Launch pair**: `cyrus_studio_public_enabled` and `cyrus_tok_live` must move TOGETHER (a public studio without the economy builds for free; the economy without the studio sells nothing). `lib/cyrus/launch-state.ts` refuses a split pair; the admin Flags tab flips both with a typed confirm.
- **Purchases from either host (r36)**: card checkouts return to the host they started on; wallet top-ups (`CYRUS_WALLET_PAY`) are idempotent by reference with a compensating refund and pending/failed states; signed purchase webhooks (`CYRUS_PURCHASE_EVENTS*`) credit tokens once; refunds and chargebacks reverse unspent tokens once (`CYRUS_CHARGEBACK_REVERSAL`). Gap: no wallet button in the tokens modal (API only), and card purchases credit directly rather than through the event path.

## Entitlement sync (r38)
Plans and tokens are Nxeon products; `GET /api/platform/cyrus/v1/entitlements` plus a signed `entitlement.changed` event feed Cyrus's **mirror** (`CYRUS_ENTITLEMENT_MIRROR`, 60 s cache, `CYRUS_ENTITLEMENT_MAX_AGE_H`), **fail closed** when unknown; reconciliation job; refunds/chargebacks reverse once; a partner-attribution hook (`CYRUS_PARTNER_ATTRIBUTION`) computes a proposal only (whether the Creator Partner Program 50%/10% applies to Cyrus plans is an open decision).

## Plan limits in the entitlement (D-63/D-64, additive)
Nxeon's entitlement (`GET /entitlements`, `entitlement.changed`) carries an optional `limits: { games, storageGb }` for the entitled tier (Free when no plan; `games` 0 = unlimited), read from Cyrus' settings (`nxeonEntitlementSources.limits`). It is informational: Cyrus enforces game slots and storage from its own config; the mirror's parser accepts it (bounded integers) and an older receiver ignores it. Contract regenerated (`tools/nxeon-platform/gen-openapi.ts`).

## Storage add-on (r51)
Extra storage is a monthly Nxeon product (`cyrus.storage.addon`), switch `CYRUS_STORAGE_ADDONS` (needs `CYRUS_STORAGE`), code `lib/cyrus/storage/addon.ts`. **Price**: the owner's per-GB bands (1 GB $0.85, 5 GB $0.75, 25 GB $0.60, 50 GB $0.30, 100 GB $0.20) in setting `cyrus_storage_price_table`; rule `cyrus_storage_pricing_rule` = `capped` (default, an ASSUMPTION pending the owner: cost(n) = min(rate(n) x n, min over higher breakpoints b of rate(b) x b), so fewer GB never cost more; 20-50 GB all cost $15.00, 67-100
- **Wallet** (default): reference `cst:<user>:g<gb>:<key>` is the wallet reference AND the idemKey (`CyrusStorageCharge.idemKey` UNIQUE), so the direct apply, the signed purchase webhook (envelope `kind: "storage"`, same receiver `/api/cyrus/purchase-events`), a redelivery, the wallet reconcile (`reconcileStorageCharges`) and the entitlement mirror apply a charge once. A failed apply after the charge refunds the wallet (compensating `:refund`).
- **Changes**: increase = the price difference for the rest of the period, charged now (rounded up); decrease or cancel = at the period end (never a mid-period refund). **Renewal**: the storage sweep charges the wallet once per period (`renew_<periodEnd ms>` key), retries a failed renewal daily for 7 days (status `past_due`, quota back to the plan's), then cancels. **Refund** of the charge in force takes its GB back. A quota drop starts a 30-day grace; nothing is deleted.

# 31 The app and the economy: one map of every customer and staff surface

What a customer or staff member can open, which code serves it, which switch gates it, and how money and entitlements flow. Detail lives in [03 studios](03-studios.md), [05 bridge and accounts](05-bridge-and-accounts.md) and [06 portals](06-portals.md); the generated lists are [reference/routes.md](reference/routes.md) (every route and page), [reference/db-tables.md](reference/db-tables.md) and [reference/flags-and-env.md](reference/flags-and-env.md).

## Surfaces
| Surface | URL | Code | Gate | Who sees it today |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **cyrus.my landing** | `cyrus.my/` | `apps/cyrus-site/**` (static, published atomically), updated landing with effect scenes built, publish pending | none | public |
| **cyrus.my app host** | `/home`, `/new`, `/account`, `/projects/<id>`, `/sign-in`, `/sign-up`, `/legal/*`, `/plans`, `/help` | `app/cyrus-host/**` rewrites (`lib/cyrus/bridge/routing.ts`, `middleware.ts`) onto the customer app tree `app/dashboard/cyrus/app/**` | `CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE`, `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` | domain mode ON in prod env; customer app ON; the studio itself only for preview accounts |
| **Studio** (forge canvas, composer, inspector) | `/dashboard/cyrus` | `components/cyrus/forge/**`, `components/cyrus/prompt/**`, `components/cyrus/live/**` | preview-access list (`preview_access_emails_modbuilder`) until the launch pair | the owner's preview accounts |
| **Plan screen** | inside New mod | `components/cyrus/app/NewModFlow.tsx`, `lib/cyrus/planner/**`, coach `CYRUS_PROMPT_COACH` | ON | preview accounts |
| **Live build panel** | studio thinking trace and project page | `components/cyrus/prompt/BuildActivity.tsx`, `lib/cyrus/builder/progress-view.ts`, `lib/cyrus/follow.ts` | needs the build image with `progress` (new service); old service renders the old step list | preview accounts |
| **Studios** | Texture, Sound, Model (viewport, editor, layers), Motion, Config, designers | `components/cyrus/studios/**`, `modelstudio/**`, `designers/**`, `config/**` | `CYRUS_CONFIG_STUDIO` ON, designers ON; plan gates | preview accounts |
| **Project page** | `/projects/<id>` | `app/dashboard/cyrus/app/projects/[rootId]/page.tsx` | customer app | revisions, builds, Test Flight verdict, "What we verified", install / rollback, configs, Get help |
| **Mod pages (community)** | `/mods/cyrus/...` | `app/(marketing)/mods/cyrus/**`, `lib/cyrus-mods/**` | `cyrus_mods_public_enabled` (absent = OFF), `cyrus_public_enabled` | 26 pages exist (24 private, 2 public); community layer empty (CP) |
| **Help center and plans** | `/cyrus-help`, `/plans` | `app/(cyrus-help)/**`, `content/cyrus/help/*.md` (27 articles), `lib/cyrus/content/**` | `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` | public once on |
| **Admin portal** | `/admin/cyrus` (secret host after the move) | `app/admin/cyrus/**` tabs: Launch, Flags, Builds, Live, Cost, Economy, Users and tokens, Reconcile, Library, Assets, Storage, Games, Learning, Notify, Audit and settings, Community | Nxeon admin RBAC (`platform` area), 2FA rule, `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST*` after the move | staff |
| **Docs viewer** | `/admin/docs/cyrus` | `app/admin/docs/cyrus/page.tsx`: lists every `docs/cyrus/**.md` (README is the index); new pages appear automatically | `requireArea("platform")` | staff |
| **Platform API** | `/api/platform/cyrus/v1/*` (grants, entitlements, webhooks) and Cyrus API v1 `/api/cyrus/v1/*` | `app/api/platform/cyrus/**`, `lib/cyrus/api/v1/**`, OpenAPI in [reference/openapi.md](reference/openapi.md) | `CYRUS_API_V1` ON, personal keys `CYRUS_API_V1_PERSONAL_KEYS` | partners |

## Identity and bridge
One Nxeon account, no Cyrus password. cyrus.my signs in through **Sign in with Nxeon**: an Ed25519-signed assertion (state and nonce bound to the starting browser, single-use jti, exact redirect, 120 s) carrying a stable subject id (never the email), verified email and role; `app/sso/cyrus/**` mints the Cyrus session. Non-CUSTOMER roles and suspended accounts are refused. "Continue with Google" for cyrus.my is built on the `feature/cyrus-google-login` worktree (uncommitted, gated by `CYRUS_GOOGLE_LOGIN`, PKCE, linked on `email_verified`), not on main. The bridge to servers is scoped grants per server through the Nxeon platform API: Cyrus never holds SSH credentials; installs go through the delivery orchestrator with rollback.

## Token economy (all numbers are settings; defaults in [29 decisions](29-decisions-and-placeholders.md))
```
 Stripe / wallet --> Nxeon (the only money system) --signed purchase + entitlement events--> Cyrus mirror (60 s cache, fails closed)
 build request --> estimate --> HOLD (reserve) --> build runs --> SETTLE at measured cost x tier multiplier --> release the rest
 ledger: CyrusTokenAccount / Lot / Ledger / Reservation, append-only, idemKey UNIQUE, sole writer lib/cyrus/tokens/ledger.ts
```
- Unit: 1 token = $0.002 of measured AI cost at the default 500 tokens per USD; Katara x1, Saka x1, Yakko x1.25; minimum 5 tokens per build.
- Sources: plan tokens (Katara 750, Saka 3,500, All models 10,000 per month; each month's tokens last 3 months; stacking), top-ups ($5-$100, 12-month expiry), game-server purchase and renewal grants (earned only for games Cyrus builds for; 90-day lots; balance cap 3,000; per-server cap 2,000; clawback 14 days), starter grant (70 tokens, 30 days).
- Caps: 5,000 tokens a day per account (1,000 for accounts younger than 7 days); our-side failures free (3 per 7 days); refused and cancelled builds charged by default.
- **Launch pair**: `cyrus_studio_public_enabled` and `cyrus_tok_live` move together or not at all (`lib/cyrus/launch-state.ts` refuses a split).
- Refunds and chargebacks reverse unspent tokens once (`CYRUS_CHARGEBACK_REVERSAL`). Stripe plan prices are found by lookup key `cyrus_plan_<tier>_v1`; the setup script refuses a live key without an override.

## Entitlements, game slots, storage
| Concern | Rule | Code |
|---|---|---|
| Plan gates | cumulative: Free builds only; Katara fast model; Saka + Sound Studio and Sound Library; All models + Texture, Model, Texture Library; Mod Packs and import are not plan-gated | `lib/cyrus/tokens/entitlement.ts`, `lib/cyrus/planner/gate.ts` |
| Game slots (D-63) | Free 1, Katara 1, Saka 3, All unlimited (placeholders); a locked game shows "Locked by plan"; the build API answers `game_slots_full` | `lib/cyrus/tokens/game-slots.ts` |
| Storage (D-64) | quotas Free 1 GB, Katara 5, Saka 25, Yakko 50; counts jars, packs, assets, revisions, drafts, uploads once per account; writes fail closed (`storage_unknown` 503, `storage_full` 507); 30-day grace after a quota drop; data never deleted automatically; monthly add-on via Nxeon | `lib/cyrus/storage/**` |
| Entitlement mirror | Nxeon is the source; Cyrus mirror fails closed when unknown; reconciliation job | `lib/cyrus/tokens/entitlement.ts`, `app/api/platform/cyrus/**` |

## What each studio costs and requires
Texture, Model and Motion are top-plan; Sound is Saka and above; designers and Config follow the plan table generated from live settings by `lib/cyrus/content/plan-table.ts`. The customer never sees model family names (a test fails if a component names them).

## Observability for staff
Admin Live (queue, capacity, breaker), Builds (release record, flight verdict), Cost (spend by lane and account, export `scripts/cyrus/cost-export.sh`), Economy (margin with `cyrus_econ_*` Stripe fee inputs), Reconcile (ledger vs Stripe vs entitlement mirror), Storage, Launch (the hourly launch-check JSON), Learning (signals and candidates).

# 30 FAQ

Short answers with the page that proves them. If an answer here and the code disagree, the code wins: fix the answer in the same change (see "Doc owners" in [14 how to work here](14-how-to-work-here.md)).

## Product
**Does Cyrus train or fine-tune AI models?** No. It calls Anthropic models and improves what surrounds them (prompts, version sheets, rules, goldens, checks, a starter bank), with a human reviewing every change. [25 training and knowledge](25-training-and-knowledge.md).

**Which games work?** Minecraft (Paper and Purpur server plugins) is built for real. Valheim, Terraria, Zomboid, Palworld, Rust, ARK and The Isle are registry rows or research with honest readiness pages. [27 games](27-games.md).

**Which Minecraft versions can it build for?** 1.21.1, 1.21.4, 1.21.8 and 1.21.11. 26.1.2, 26.2 and 26.3 are previews and cannot be built until the 26.x readiness steps are done and the owner flips one. [27 games](27-games.md), [reference/versions.md](reference/versions.md).

**Do players have to install anything?** Not for plugins. A custom look or sound is delivered as a server resource pack that players accept on join. Client mods (Fabric, NeoForge) are not offered. [24 techniques](24-techniques-catalogue.md).

**Can it make a full-auto gun / a shader / a new block model?** Full-auto needs a client mod (the client repeats a held click only every 4 ticks and sends no held state). Shaders, free HUD positioning and new entity or block models are outside what a server can do; the plan screen says so before tokens are spent. [24 techniques](24-techniques-catalogue.md).

**How many custom creatures can one mod have?** Four per server, each up to 32 bones, 64 cubes and 8 animation clips (`lib/cyrus/creature/spec.ts`). Server side only; nobody has verified the look in a real client. [24 techniques](24-techniques-catalogue.md).

**Why did my mod "succeed" but a lane did not ship?** The plan promised a lane (for example a creature) and the model or a gate left it out. Since rc13 every missing planned lane is a visible "Planned but not delivered" card and a summary notice. [22 life of a build](22-life-of-a-build.md).

**What does "What we verified" mean?** The highest rung reached: static (compiled and checked), synthetic (MockBukkit pre-flight), booted (real Test Flight), behaviour (oracle / playtest on a real server). Client verification is never claimed. [16 behaviour oracle](16-behaviour-oracle.md), [25](25-training-and-knowledge.md).

## Money
**What does a build cost?** Measured: about $0.15 for plain code, $0.27 designer, $0.37 sound, $0.44 texture, up to about $0.8-1.3 for creature batches; the customer pays measured cost x tier multiplier in tokens (1 token = $0.002 at the default 500 per USD), minimum 5 tokens. [22](22-life-of-a-build.md), [31](31-app-and-economy.md).

**Is anything charged when our side fails?** No, within a fair-use limit (3 per rolling 7 days). Refused and cancelled builds are charged by default. A change request is a new build. [31](31-app-and-economy.md).

**Are prices final?** No. Token price, plan sizes, game slots and storage quotas are agent placeholders until the owner decides. [29 decisions](29-decisions-and-placeholders.md).

## Operations
**How do I know whether Cyrus is ready to launch?** `scripts/cyrus/launch-check.sh public` prints GO or NO-GO with the fix for each gap. [28 handbook](28-operations-handbook.md).

**How do I deploy?** Portal: `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`, look, `scripts/promote-production.sh`. Build service: `deploy-modbuilder.sh` with an idle service. Never build in `/opt/nxeon`. [28](28-operations-handbook.md), [CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK](../CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK.md).

**How do I roll back?** Portal: `scripts/rollback-release.sh --production [RELEASE_ID]` (swaps the release symlink; worker and schema are not rolled back). Image: the deploy script restores the previous tag. Flags: set them back; the launch pair is closed with the typed confirmation `CLOSE CYRUS`. [28](28-operations-handbook.md).

**Which version of the build service is running?** Git cannot tell. Ask the VM (`docker ps`) or `GET /health` through the tunnel. [23 build service](23-build-service.md).

**A build has been quiet for minutes. Is it stuck?** Usually not: the model is thinking (57-78% of output tokens are thinking). # 30 FAQ

Short answers with the page that proves them. If an answer here and the code disagree, the code wins: fix the answer in the same change (see "Doc owners" in [14 how to work here](14-how-to-work-here.md)).

## Product
**Does Cyrus train or fine-tune AI models?** No. It calls Anthropic models and improves what surrounds them (prompts, version sheets, rules, goldens, checks, a starter bank), with a human reviewing every change. [25 training and knowledge](25-training-and-knowledge.md).

**Which games work?** Minecraft (Paper and Purpur server plugins) is built for real. Valheim, Terraria, Zomboid, Palworld, Rust, ARK and The Isle are registry rows or research with honest readiness pages. [27 games](27-games.md).

**Which Minecraft versions can it build for?** 1.21.1, 1.21.4, 1.21.8 and 1.21.11. 26.1.2, 26.2 and 26.3 are previews and cannot be built until the 26.x readiness steps are done and the owner flips one. [27 games](27-games.md), [reference/versions.md](reference/versions.md).

**Do players have to install anything?** Not for plugins. A custom look or sound is delivered as a server resource pack that players accept on join. Client mods (Fabric, NeoForge) are not offered. [24 techniques](24-techniques-catalogue.md).

**Can it make a full-auto gun / a shader / a new block model?** Full-auto needs a client mod (the client repeats a held click only every 4 ticks and sends no held state). Shaders, free HUD positioning and new entity or block models are outside what a server can do; the plan screen says so before tokens are spent. [24 techniques](24-techniques-catalogue.md).

**How many custom creatures can one mod have?** Four per server, each up to 32 bones, 64 cubes and 8 animation clips (`lib/cyrus/creature/spec.ts`). Server side only; nobody has verified the look in a real client. [24 techniques](24-techniques-catalogue.md).

**Why did my mod "succeed" but a lane did not ship?** The plan promised a lane (for example a creature) and the model or a gate left it out. Since rc13 every missing planned lane is a visible "Planned but not delivered" card and a summary notice. [22 life of a build](22-life-of-a-build.md).

Client verification is never claimed. [16 behaviour oracle](16-behaviour-oracle.md), [25](25-training-and-knowledge.md).

**What does a build cost?** Measured: about $0.15 for plain code, $0.27 designer, $0.37 sound, $0.44 texture, up to about $0.8-1.3 for creature batches; the customer pays measured cost x tier multiplier in tokens (1 token = $0.002 at the default 500 per USD), minimum 5 tokens. [22](22-life-of-a-build.md), [31](31-app-and-economy.md).

**Is anything charged when our side fails?** No, within a fair-use limit (3 per rolling 7 days). Refused and cancelled builds are charged by default. A change request is a new build. [31](31-app-and-economy.md).

# 20 Documentation coverage matrix

Which page documents which subsystem, how deep, how stale it was, and what was mismatched against the code. Written 2026-10-15 by the documentation lead (task CZ); the "before" column is the audit of `main` at `89608a9f` (rc16) and the "after" column is this branch. It is the checklist to re-run after big releases, and the **Status snapshot** at the end is the branch and image state that every other page's "merged / not merged" words must agree with.

Depth scale: **none** (not written down) / **stub** (a mention) / **adequate** (a reader can act, gaps known) / **complete** (verifiable, with limits, numbers, code paths and tests). Generated references (`reference/*`) are rebuilt from code by `scripts/cyrus/docs-build.ts` and guarded by `test/cyrus-docs-coverage.test.ts`; "complete" for a hand-written page means the facts were checked against code on the date above, not that they cannot drift: the owner map [reference/doc-owners.md](reference/doc-owners.md) says which pages a code change obliges you to review.

Depth scale: **none** (not written down) / **stub** (a mention) / **adequate** (a reader can act, gaps known) / **complete** (verifiable, with limits, numbers, code paths and tests). #!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
#
# Rules: /root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md. The node-2 copy is a build/run sandbox,
# not a place to edit or commit — your primary-side worktree stays the source of truth.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${DEVHOST_REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"

die() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; }
q() { printf '%q ' "$@"; }
