# CZ: complete Cyrus documentation set (2026-10-15)

Branch `feature/cyrus-docs-complete` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-docs-complete`, from main `89608a9f` = rc16). Docs, generator and test only. Nothing deployed, no flag, no migration. Rebased conflicts to expect: `docs/cyrus/README.md` and `06-portals.md` (rc17 adds the 18-seo row); take both.

## What was built
New hand-written pages (numbers 20+; 18-19 reserved for SEO on `release/cyrus-rc17`):
20 coverage matrix (+ mismatch register + status snapshot), 21 infrastructure (ASCII diagram), 22 life of a build (mermaid sequence, measured timings and costs), 23 build service, 24 techniques catalogue, 25 training and knowledge, 26 assets taxonomy, 27 games, 28 operations handbook (incl. the 2026-10-15 scraper outage), 29 decisions / placeholders / switches by name, 30 FAQ, 31 app and economy. README and 00-overview rewritten with a reading order by role; 14 gained "Doc owners".

Generated (zero model tokens, `scripts/cyrus/docs-build.ts`): `reference/infra-units.md`, `reference/build-service.md`, `reference/limits.md`, `reference/doc-owners.md`; the flags reference now includes the build-service switches (`CYRUS_REMOTE_FLAGS`) and every env/setting name has a meaning.

Machine-readable: `docs/cyrus/_data/doc-owners.json` (`{version:1, rules:[{paths, docs}]}`, 23 rules) for the release-train agent.

Guards (`test/cyrus-docs-coverage.test.ts`, new describe + 1 new test): empty flag meaning, dead rule or missing doc in doc-owners, unowned `lib/cyrus/<dir>` or `services/modbuilder/*.js`, service module not copied by the Dockerfile, missing complete-set pages. `scripts/cyrus/docs-links.ts [--paths]`: relative links + headings + cited repo paths in pages 20+.

## Coverage matrix, before and after (49 concerns, full table in docs/cyrus/20-coverage-matrix.md)
| Depth | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| none | 4 | 0 |
| stub | 6 | 0 |
| adequate | 27 | 9 |
| complete | 12 | 40 |
Before-state "none": systemd units/timers, life of a build, taxonomy, FAQ-class material; "stub": sound relay, host capacity, models/routing/effort, vanilla technique catalogue, community state, SEO.
Still "adequate" after: studios (03), security (08), SEO (pointer only until rc17), community mod pages (empty in production), legal (drafts on a worktree), vanilla technique catalogue (research input), universal-modder KB (private), game readiness snapshots (dated 2026-10-08), disk/memory capacity (a dated report).

## Mismatches found against the code (all fixed unless noted)
1. 46 "not merged / NOT deployed" labels on branches that are in main (02, 04, 06, 09, 12, features.json). 11-history keeps its as-of-date wording plus a reading note.
2. Admin Flags text said MB_PREFLIGHT default `1` = enforce; code default is `advise` (rc15). Fixed in `lib/cyrus/admin/flags.ts` text only.
3. 02 said 50 rules `rules-2026-10-12.3`, "only 0.4 running", service history 0.3-0.6; repo has 55 rules `rules-2026-10-13.1`; tags 0.19-0.22 exist in notes. Running tag cannot be known from git (documented how to read it).
4. 07: root disk "11 GB free" (87% / 6.5 GB on 2026-10-15); tank "3.6 TB single disk" vs ZFS 2.6 TB: noted as unverified.
5. The flags generator ignored `CYRUS_REMOTE_FLAGS`, leaving 47 env/setting names without meaning; fixed (+ `flag-notes.json`).
6. `rollback-release.sh` and the release-symlink model had zero mentions; "blue/green" does not exist.
7. No backup docs for Dropbox, timers, stagger; 2026-10-15 incident not in the incident table.
8. features.json lacked 12 recent features (live progress, oracle, pre-flight/ledger, boss model, speed, capacity, Spyglass, publish-check, library prod, offsite backups, dispatch, launch check).
9. Two items numbered 18 in 12.
10. NOT fixed (reported): `feature/cyrus-legal`, `-google-login`, `-community`, `-library-taxonomy`, `-more-mobs` have tip == main with UNCOMMITTED work in their worktrees, so a naive "is merged" check wrongly says merged. No baseline.json / gate-accepted.json exists, so the eval gate is `no-reference`.

## Facts worth the owner's attention (verified here)
- Production env (names, 0/1 only): launch pair absent = OFF; `CYRUS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET` are set but `CYRUS_GOOGLE_LOGIN` is absent and the login code is not on main (inert); library backend/browse/contribute ON and the catalogue is loaded (62,777 / 1,145,478 rows per CP).
- Build-service `MB_*` values live on the VM and were not readable: marked unverified in 29.
- rc17 (5 commits ahead of main) holds mega-staging + technical SEO and is not on main.
- Alerts have no webhook; nginx list guard, DB role and backup stagger from the hardening report are owner steps.

## Verification
- `NODE_PATH=/opt/nxeon/node_modules /opt/nxeon/node_modules/.bin/tsx scripts/cyrus/docs-build.ts` regenerated all references; `docs-links.ts --paths` ok (121 pages, cited paths verified).
- tsc and `test/cyrus-docs-coverage.test.ts` through `scripts/devhost`: see the final message of the task for results.
- Not verified: the live state of production beyond what is cited; numbers in 21 capacity come from the NX hardening report of the same day.

One-page owner summary **What I recommend, in plain words** 1. **Cyrus gets its own accounts, created the moment someone first uses Cyrus.** Not at Nxeon sign-up. A Nxeon customer never "signs up for Cyrus": they click **Sign in with Nxeon** on cyrus.my (or **Open Cyrus** in the Nxeon portal), approve once, and they are in. Behind that one click Cyrus creates their Cyrus account and remembers that it belongs to that Nxeon account. To the customer it feels exactly like your id 2. **People who only want Cyrus can sign up on cyrus.my with Google or email + password**, without a Nxeon account. Later they can press **Connect Nxeon** to use their servers. (Today, Continue with Google on cyrus.my secretly creates a *Nxeon* account. That changes.) 3. **Nxeon is the identity provider ("Sign in with Nxeon") using the standard protocol (OpenID Connect).** Cyrus is a normal client of it, like Kodely. Nxeon keeps knowing only "this customer allowed Cyrus, on these servers". Cyrus keeps knowing only "this Cyrus account is linked to Nxeon customer X". 4. **Cyrus reaches a customer's server only through Nxeon's API, with the customer's per-server permission**, never with SSH keys. Nxeon stays the owner of everything that is installed on its servers. 5. **The Nxeon portal keeps its Cyrus features** (create a mod for this server, see your Cyrus mods, install, token balance) as native Nxeon screens that pull from the Cyrus API, plus an **Open Cyrus** button for the full studio. If Cyrus is down, those panels say so and the rest of Nxeon works. 6. **Money**: Cyrus should sell its own plans through its **own Stripe account under its own company** (Stripe lets you hold several accounts in one organisation). The Nxeon wallet can stay as a payment option for token packs. Decide this before Cyrus takes real payments: today the paid economy is still switched off (launch pair off), so the move costs almost nothing now and a lot later. 7. **Its own code repository, database, server and admin.** Cyrus moves to a new GitHub repository with its history, its own Postgres, its own virtual machine on your Proxmox (a Nxeon VPS that Cyrus "rents"), and its admin on a secret `*.cyrus.my` address behind Cloudflare Access. ``` Nxeon customer Cyrus-only person | | | nxeon.cloud (portal) | cyrus.my (app) v v +------------------------+ OpenID Connect +--------------------------+ | NXEON (company A) | "Sign in with | CYRUS (company B) | | accounts, wallet, | Nxeon" ---------> | own accounts (JIT), | | servers, Nxeon admin | id_token + sub | identities: nxeon/google/| | | | password, own sessions | | Platform API v1 <-----+--- user-granted ----+ installs mods on servers | | (per-server grants, | OAuth token | it was allowed to touch | | install manifests) | | | | | | Cyrus API v1 <----------+-- Nxeon portal panels | Cyrus panels (native)--+--- service token + -> (projects, builds, | (cached, fail-soft) | + "Open Cyrus" button | signed subject | tokens, installs) | | | <-- signed webhooks-+ build.finished, install.. | | DB: nxeon | | DB: cyrus (own Postgres) | | Stripe: Nxeon account | | Stripe: Cyrus account | | admin: secret nxeon | | admin: .cyrus.my | +------------------------+ +--------------------------+ ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph N[Nxeon - nxeon.cloud] NA[Accounts + sessions] --> OP[OIDC provider

# DD: Cyrus traffic and product analytics (2026-10-15)

Branch `feature/cyrus-analytics` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-analytics`), 2 commits on top of main `b447360d` (rebased after the SEO vhost fixes landed). Not merged, not deployed, not published, nothing applied to nginx or the database, `/opt/nxeon` untouched. Full page in the repo: `docs/cyrus/21-analytics.md`.

## What exists now vs before
| Need | Before (verified) | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Cyrus web traffic in the admin | none; 8 `Visit` rows touched Cyrus paths in 7 days | `/admin/cyrus/analytics` (tab "Analytics", ADMIN), 9 sections, 7/30/90 days, filters plan / source / country / device / human only |
| cyrus.my vs nxeon.cloud | `Visit` had no host column | `Visit.host` + `Visit.product` (`cyrus`/`nxeon`, NULL = legacy, no backfill) written by `/api/track` |
| Static landing | no beacon, invisible | `apps/cyrus-site/src/assets/js/a.js`, 2,023 bytes, first party, `sendBeacon` to `/api/cyrus/analytics/hit` |
| Cyrus app pages on cyrus.my | `/api/track` is not reachable there (middleware 404s POST) | `CyrusTracker` in the host shell, sign-in/up and legal pages, same endpoint |
| AI-assistant referrals | none | referrer host + `utm_source` (chatgpt.com, chat.openai.com, perplexity, claude.ai, gemini, copilot, you.com, phind, meta-ai, grok, deepseek, mistral, poe, duck-ai, kagi) |
| Attribution / conversions | 0 rows (flags off) | unchanged and still off; the suite reads `CyrusAttribution` for account sources when it fills |
| Funnel / cohorts / retention / prompt analytics | none | landing funnel (page loads), ordered account funnel with medians, weekly cohorts D1/D7/D30, product and money sections |
| Export / API / digest | none | CSV per table + JSON (`/api/admin/cyrus/analytics`, audited), weekly digest (off) |

## What it measures and how (all human-only, bots counted apart)
1. **Collection.** Beacon events once per page load: `view`, `scroll50`, `scroll90`, `prompt_focus`, `prompt_submit` (no text), `plans_view`, `signin_click`, `signup_click`. Body: path, referrer hostname, UTM, webdriver flag; with analytics consent also a random 30 day id (`cyrus_vid`), session id and `?ref=`.
2. **Server rules** (`decideHit`, pure, tested): flag off -> 204; `DNT: 1` / `Sec-GPC: 1` -> dropped before anything; same-origin only; consent read from the cookie server side; bots (UA catalogue, datacenter/flagged IP, webdriver) only counted (`CyrusDailyMetrics web.bot_hits`, batched); IP and UA never stored (country + device class derived, address discarded).
3. **Product events** from existing facts, no new write path: first Cyrus sign-in (`ActivityEvent auth.login` method `nxeon-sso`/`google-cyrus`), signup/new-to-Nxeon (`User.createdAt` within 24 h), username (`CyrusCreator`), first prompt/build (`ModBuild`), build ok/failed by lane/errorCode/model (`ModBuild`, `cyrus.assets.planned.lanes`), Test Flight verdict (`cyrus.testFlight

## Metric definitions (also printed on the Data quality tab, one source: `lib/cyrus/analytics/definitions.ts`)
- **Human page view**: beacon hit, not bot, not webdriver, no DNT/GPC (same human rule as `/admin/conversion`, parity pinned by a test).
- **Visitor**: distinct rotating anonymous id, a consented SAMPLE, never extrapolated. Unique visitors for people who declined do not exist by design (no identifier); they are page views.
- **Landing funnel**: page loads that did the thing (each event sent at most once per load).
- **Account funnel**: first sign-in, username, first build, first success, first install, paid. Counted at a step if reached or any later step; medians from in-order pairs only; skipped and out-of-order counts shown.
- **Activated**: at least one succeeded build. North star shown separately: median time first seen -> first install and share within 24 h.
- **First try**: succeeded with `attempts = 1` (0 = unknown, never counted). **Success rate**: succeeded / (succeeded + failed).
- **Abandoned build**: failed/cancelled and no build by the account within 24 h. **Plan abandoned**: `plan_shown` with no build within 30 min.
- **Cohort Dn**: share of ELIGIBLE accounts (a whole day n has passed) that built on exactly day n after first seen; `Dn+` = day n or later; counts printed.
- **Revenue**: live-mode ledger purchases; test mode apart. **MRR**: last paid plan invoice of each live active subscription (no list price); those without are excluded and counted. **Margin**: revenue - measured AI cost - estimated card fees; cost on accounts that never paid shown.
- **Excluded**: staff accounts and `cyrus_analytics_exclude_users`.

# DB: Cyrus marketing roadmap, built from what Nxeon actually did (2026-10-15)

Status: RESEARCH and PLANNING only. No code, no DNS, no send, no post, nothing under /opt/nxeon edited. Production DB was read with SELECT-only aggregate queries (read-only transaction, no PII written here; partners and creators are counted, not named).

How to read this: every number is tagged. **(DB)** = measured from the Nxeon production DB on 2026-10-15, window 2026-07-23 to 2026-10-15 (about 12 weeks; the site is young). **(note)** = from an agent note or docs file. **(web)** = from a fetched or searched page with the URL given. **(proposal)** = my suggestion with no benchmark behind it. **UNKNOWN** = nothing I read answer

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 0. The five things to take away

1. **Nxeon never had a traffic-quality problem it could see, then a conversion problem it could not fix.** Raw sessions in the week of 2026-10-05 were 80,003, human sessions 1,141, human visitors 671, signups 85, deployed 28, paid 4 (DB, GrowthReport). About 98.6 percent of raw sessions were non-human. Until the bot classifier shipped (2026-10-01) every top-of-funnel number Nxe
2. **The one channel that worked was not planned: AI assistants.** ChatGPT is the first touch of 31.9 percent of human, non-mod entry visits (1,583 of 4,969, 90 days) and of 402 of 1,019 signups in the last 110 days (DB). It cites concrete, factual pages (free Minecraft, pricing, game hosting), not generic content. For Cyrus, "be the page ChatGPT cites for 'AI Minecraft plugin 
3. **Volume without a path to a paid action converts at about zero.** The free-intent landing pages produced 83 signups and 0 servers (friction report, 14 days); of 108 free Minecraft servers only 19 (17.6 percent) were ever woken, 4 (3.7 percent) reached multiplayer, and 2 owners paid (DB). Cyrus's equivalent is: a signup who never gets a mod installed on a server and joined b
4. **Scaled, templated pages hurt Nxeon.** ~65,000 near-templated mod pages went live in about a week and Google stopped crawling them within days (analysis note 2026-10-06; 28 search-referred visits across 64,853 mod pages in 30 days). Cyrus's community mod and library pages must be a quality-gated trickle, not a flood.
5. **Creators want money up front, not commission.** Of 49 creators who answered Nxeon's partner outreach, 26 said no to commission, 15 quoted flat rates between $100 and $5,000, others asked for CPM of $10 to $25 (note, creator-fixed-fee CSV). The 50 percent first-purchase discount plus 40 percent commission programme produced 290 clicks, 18 signups, 2 paying customers and $6.

Also load-bearing and easy to miss: **Cyrus has zero real external users today** (1 token account, 23 projects, 1 user, 26 mod pages of which 2 are public, no waitlist exists, the private beta allow-list has 2 emails; DB). Everything in sections 4 and 5 starts from absolute zero. And **the plan prices are placeholders ("to be announced")**, so no price-based message or paid-acq
